NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,

AUG 28 1939

Japanese Want Custody
Of Interned Soldiers

Mr. Y. Miura Asks for
List of Names, Arms

Japanese authorities were dissatisfied with the attitude of the Settlement authorities toward demands for the custody of Chinese soldiers interned in the Settlement at a time when the Shanghai area is under Japanese occupation, the Tai-ku Shimpo said yesterday.

In reply to a demand from Mr. Yoshiaki Miura, Japanese Consul-General, for a list of the prisoners and their arms, the Settlement authorities on Saturday reported only on those who came into the Settlement after the famous siege at the Joint Savings' Society godown on North Szechuen Road, the paper said.

The Japanese authorities wanted information not only about those men but also about the 6,000 to 7,000 soldiers who were reported to have filtered into the Settlement and Concession at the time of the hostilities. The Japanese desired information about their whereabouts and their arms, according to the paper.

Criticism

It was a matter for criticism, the paper stated, that more than 230 Chinese troops who had served under Hsieh Chun-yuan of the Central Army 88th Division were still being kept in prisoners' barracks at Kiaochow and Singapore Roads, now that the second anniversary of the Shanghai fighting had passed.

Whether they were being fed at the expense of the Shanghai Municipal Council or the Chungking Government was not the only question for the Japanese authorities, the paper declared. The fact that the Chinese had not yet been handed over to the Japanese was a matter for a great concern, according to the daily.

REPORT ON SOLDIERS
HERE IS DESIRED

Japanese Wish Custody
Of Chinese Interned
In Settlement

Japanese authorities were dissatisfied with the attitude of the Settlement authorities towards demands for the custody of Chinese soldiers interned in the Settlement at a time when the Shanghai area is under Japanese occupation, the "Tairiku Shimpo" said yesterday.

In reply to a demand from Mr. Yoshiaki Miura, Japanese Consul-General, for a list of the prisoners and their arms, the Settlement authorities on Saturday reported only on those who came into the Settlement after the famous siege at the Joint Savings' Society go-down on North Szechuen Road, the paper said.

The Japanese authorities wanted information not only about those men but also about the 6,000 to 7,000 soldiers who were reported to have filtered into the Settlement and Concession at the time of the hostilities. The Japanese desired information about their whereabouts and their arms, according to the paper.

It was a matter for criticism, the paper stated, that more than 230 Chinese troops which had served under Hsien Chin-yuan of the Central Army 88th Division were still being kept in prisoners' barracks at Kiaochow and Singapore Roads, now that the second anniversary of the Shanghai fighting had passed.

Whether they were being fed at the expense of the Shanghai Municipal Council or the Chungking Government was not the only question for the Japanese authorities, the paper declared.

The fact that the Chinese had not yet been handed over to the Japanese was a matter for a great concern, according to the daily.

“Lone Battalion” Comdr.
Answers Local Paper

Colonel Hsieh Claims Chungking Has Reimbursed
The Council With Sums; Calls For Just And
Humanitarian Treatment Of Troops

In connection with the allegation
made by the “Ta-Kung Shunpo” that
the maintenance of members of the
Lone Battalion is a charge upon
the finances of the
Shanghai Municipal Council, a
statement was issued by Col. Hsieh
Cheng-yuan, the battalion com-
mander, refuting the allegation yes-
terday.

In the period between October 23,
1937, and November 30, 1938, Col.
Hsieh stated, members of the “Lone
Battalion” were supported by local
Chinese charitable organizations and
by public contributions. During the
nine month period from December,
1938, to August 1939, a monthly
sum of $4,500 has been drawn from
the S.M.C. for the maintenance of
the “Lone Battalion”, making a total
of $40,500, for which receipts had
been issued by him, he stated. The
Chinese Government in Chungking
had reimbursed the Council with a
sum of $43,500 some time during
April, so that a sum of $3,000 is
still outstanding in favour of the
“Lone Battalion,” the statement re-
vealed.

Cites Cases Of Internment

The statement then cited various
precedents in which neutral States
had accorded just and humanitarian
treatment to troops belonging to the
contestants, under the provisions of
the usually recognized international
law. The expenses for the upkeep
of the belligerent would be repaid
only after peace had been conclud-
ed between the contestants.

Among other examples, Col.
Hsieh cited the case of the Franco-
Prussian War of 1871, during which
Switzerland had interned more than
80,000 French troops. When the
Franco-Prussian War was conclud-
ed, France repaid Switzerland a
sum of Fr. 1,000,000, representing
expenses laid out for the upkeep
of interned French troops. A simi-
lar precedent was also afforded
during the World War when troops
belonging to the contestants were
also interned in Switzerland.

“Our withdrawal from the go-
downs of the Joint Savings Society
and Trust in October, 1937, was
made in compliance with the re-
quest of third parties, and under
such circumstance the Lone Batta-
lion could not be regarded as run-
away soldiers,” Col. Hsieh main-
tained.

Whether or not it would be pos-
sible in the future to refund the
expenses for the upkeep of the
Lone Battalion to the S.M.C., it is
hardly possible for me to say he
added.

“But what I had long wished to
say is that Hongkew should be im-
mediately restored to the Shanghai
Municipal Council, and the restric-
tions that have been placed in the
surrounding areas of the Settle-
ment should be immediately remov-
ed so that the financial position of
the Council might be eased.”

“孤军”指挥官
答复本地报纸

谢团长称重庆方面已向工部局偿还款项；呼吁给予部队公正和人道待遇

针对《大公报》（Ta-Kung Shunpo）指控“孤军”成员的给养费用由上海公共租界工部局财政承担一事，该团指挥官谢晋元上校昨日发表声明，驳斥了这一指控。

谢上校称，在1937年10月23日至1938年11月30日期间，“孤军”成员由当地中国慈善机构和公众捐款供养。在1938年12月至1939年8月的九个月期间，每月从上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）支取4,500美元用于“孤军”的给养，总计40,500美元，他表示已就此出具收据。声明透露，重庆的中国政府曾在四月间的某个时候向工部局偿还了43,500美元，因此仍有3,000美元未结清，这笔款项有利于“孤军”。

引用拘禁案例

声明随后引用了各种先例，说明中立国根据通常公认的国际法条款，对交战方所属部队给予了公正和人道的待遇。只有在交战双方达成和平之后，才会偿还维持交战方人员的费用。

除其他示例外，谢上校还引用了1871年普法战争期间的案例，当时瑞士拘禁了8万多名法国士兵。当普法战争结束时，法国向瑞士偿还了100万法郎，作为维持被拘禁法国士兵费用的补偿。在世界大战期间也出现了类似的先例，当时交战双方的部队也被拘禁在瑞士。

“我们于1937年10月从四行联合储蓄信托仓库撤出，是应第三方的请求而进行的，在这种情况下，‘孤军’不能被视为逃兵，”谢上校坚持认为。

至于将来是否有可能向上海公共租界工部局退还维持“孤军”的费用，他补充说，我很难说。

“但我一直想说的是，虹口应立即归还给上海公共租界工部局，并应立即取消在租界周边地区实施的限制，以便缓解工部局的财政状况。”

pages.en:
“Lone Battalion” Head
Claims Privileges

Government Will Pay for
Support of Internees

In reply to the Japanese accusation that the Shanghai Municipal Council has been feeding members of the Chinese “Lone Battalion” encamped in Kiaochow Road without being compensated by the Chinese government, Colonel Hsieh Chung-nan, commander of the battalion who made world-wide fame by offering many days’ resistance against the Japanese at Chapei after all other units of Chinese troops had withdrawn, issued a statement through the Sheng Sheng News Agency last night.

Colonel Hsieh stated that he and his men withdrew from Chapei by order from the Chinese high command only at the request of British and American military leaders in Shanghai. Between the date of withdrawal (October 31, 1937) and November of last year they had been fed by Chinese philanthropic bodies. During the past nine months he had been borrowing $4,500 monthly from the Shanghai Municipal Council and the debt amounted to $40,500. The Council has requested the Chinese government to refund this debt and the latter complied with the request in April by sending $43,600. At present the Chinese government has deposited $3,100 with the Council for feeding the battalion, Colonel Hsieh stated.

Quoting international law and precedents in world politics, Colonel Hsieh contended that the money used by neutrals for feeding war prisoners should be refunded by the country concerned after the armistice. He mentioned Switzerland during the Franco-Prussian War (1871) as an example. France was said to have returned the necessary funds only after the war during which Switzerland had been caring for more than 80,000 French troops. He wished to make it clear that he and his men could not be treated as “escaped soldiers.”

While the Japanese have threatened to refuse to pay taxes to the Council if the latter continues to spend money on the “Lone Battalion,” Colonel Hsieh concluded by suggesting that the Council take over Hongkew and Japanese-controlled parts of the Settlement in order to increase its revenues.

“孤军”首领
声称享有特权

政府将支付被拘禁者的给养费用

针对日本方面指责上海公共租界工部局在未得到中国政府补偿的情况下，一直在为驻扎在胶州路的中国“孤军”成员提供食物，谢晋南上校昨晚通过生生通讯社发表声明予以回应。谢上校曾在中国军队其他部队撤离后，在闸北对日军进行了多日的抵抗，从而闻名世界。

谢上校称，他和他的部下是应英美军事领导人在上海的请求，仅根据中国最高指挥部的命令从闸北撤离的。从撤离之日（1937年10月31日）到去年11月期间，他们的食物由中国慈善机构提供。在过去九个月里，他每月向上海公共租界工部局借款4,500美元，债务总额达40,500美元。工部局已要求中国政府偿还这笔债务，后者于四月间汇来43,600美元以响应这一请求。谢上校称，目前中国政府已向工部局存入3,100美元，用于该团的给养。

谢上校援引国际法和世界政治中的先例，辩称中立国用于供养战俘的资金应在停战后由相关国家偿还。他提到普法战争（1871年）期间的瑞士作为一个例子。据说法国直到战争结束后才归还必要资金，在此期间瑞士一直照料着8万多名法国士兵。他希望澄清，他和他的部下不能被当作“逃兵”对待。

尽管日本人威胁说，如果工部局继续花钱供养“孤军”，他们将拒绝向工部局纳税，但谢上校最后建议工部局接管虹口及租界内由日本人控制的区域，以增加其收入。

drain upon the already-depleted

of several hundred ex-Chinese
soldiers interned in the Interna-

in a featured article.

fence sector when the Japanese

at the corner of Kiaochow and
Singapore Roads. They first num-

daily.
Their maintenance cost was first
paid by the Chinese Nationalist
Government, but since the fall of

the costs of their internment. “The

day by the Chungking Government,
although there is no possibility of
that regime making any payments,”
according to the newspaper.

Indignation has been caused
among Japanese, the daily claimed,
because of the action of the Coun-
cil “in protecting and maintaining
Chinese prisoners for such a long
time in an area under Japanese
control.”
Several casualties were caused
last year in a riot at the camp
when the internees resisted an at-
tempt by the Russian Regiment,
S.V.C., to prevent them from hoist-
ing a Chinese nationalist flag, the
paper recalled.
The “Tariku Shimpo” failed to
state what should be done with
the internees.

《上海泰晤士报》
1939年8月16日
日本抗议“孤军”给养问题
若囚犯由工部局财政收入供养，上海日本纳税人可能不久将拒绝纳税

据本地日文日报《大陆新报》（Tariku Shimpo）昨日在一篇特写文章中报道，由于数百名前中国士兵被拘禁在国际租界内，据称导致上海公共租界工部局本已枯竭的财政遭受沉重负担，日本纳税人可能很快会停止缴纳税款。

1937年10月日军占领闸北时，通过英军防区逃入租界的“孤军”中国成员，一直被拘禁在胶州路与新加坡路拐角处的一个营地中。据该日报称，他们最初人数为230人。

《大陆新报》称，他们的给养费用最初由中国国民政府支付，但自南京落入日军手中以来，没有任何资金前来支付他们的拘禁费用。“工部局希望有朝一日能从重庆政府获得偿还，尽管该政权付款的可能性微乎其微，”该报称。

回顾骚乱

该日报声称，日本人的愤怒是由工部局“在日本控制区域内如此长时间地保护和维持中国囚犯”的行为引起的。

该报回顾说，去年营地里发生了一场骚乱，造成数人伤亡，当时被拘禁者抵抗了上海义勇队（S.V.C.）俄国团阻止他们升起中国国民党旗帜的企图。

《大陆新报》未说明应对这些被拘禁者采取何种措施。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

AUG 1 6 1939

The Lone Battalion
One of the most difficult of the many
problems left over from the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in the Shanghai area and one which
is incapable of solution until peace is declared
involves the "Lone Battalion," now interned
in Kiaochow Road. These men, after a heroic
struggle against the Japanese, were offered the
sanctuary of the Foreign Settlement, and those
who could walk, hobble or be carried out of
the Joint Savings Bank building, were admitted
into the Settlement and afterwards interned
until their disposition could be arranged. Unfortunately, the tide of war passed Shanghai
and swept up the Yangtze beyond Hankow, and
with Shanghai surrounded by Japanese troops
there is no possibility of releasing them.
Theoretically, they could be marched to the
edge of the Settlement and escorted across the
border, but as the Japanese are in control, and
as the time of the Shanghai fighting were in
no mood to burden themselves with prisoners,
this is impossible. Continued internment therefore becomes necessary. At the time of the
"Lone Battalion" incident, the country rang
with their fame. Their brave conduct and
heroic deeds would never be forgotten, it was
declared. Apparently, the Chungking Government's memory is lapsing because for some
months no money has been forthcoming for
their upkeep, and the larger part now falls on
the Municipal Council. The action of the
foreign authorities has been a dual cause of
complaint. The Japanese objected to this
humanitarian intervention, and after some time
in internment serious trouble broke out among
the internees, necessitating strong action to
suppress it. Now, the local Japanese official
organ has opened a campaign against them
and reports that Japanese ratepayers may refuse to pay their rates if the drain on municipal finances for their upkeep is to be maintained. It is a question of Solomonic perplexity,
and the clamant Japanese ratepayers can be
assured that the Municipal Council is as anxious as anybody to solve it, but nobody has yet
offered the means of doing it. Neither does
the Japanese newspaper which inspires the
clamour. It is one of those difficulties which
the Council must continue to endure until
peace once again rules in this country.

《字林西报》

1939年8月16日

孤军

在上海地区中日敌对行动遗留下来的众多问题中，最棘手且除非宣布和平否则无法解决的问题之一，涉及目前被拘禁在胶州路的“孤军”。这些人在与日军进行英勇斗争后，获得了外国租界的庇护，那些能够行走、蹒跚或被抬出四行储蓄银行大楼的人被允许进入租界，随后被拘禁，直到安排好对他们的处置。不幸的是，战争的浪潮掠过上海，席卷长江直至汉口以外，随着上海被日军包围，释放他们已无可能。

理论上，可以将他们行进至租界边缘并护送过境，但由于日军处于控制地位，且上海战斗时期的日军无意承担囚犯的负担，这是不可能的。因此，继续拘禁成为必要。在“孤军”事件发生时，全国上下都传颂着他们的名声。人们宣称，他们的勇敢行为和英雄事迹永远不会被遗忘。显然，重庆政府的记忆正在衰退，因为几个月来没有资金前来支付他们的给养费用，现在大部分负担落到了工部局身上。外国当局的行为引起了双重抱怨。日本人反对这种人道主义干预，而在拘禁一段时间后，被拘禁者内部发生了严重麻烦，不得不采取强力行动予以镇压。现在，当地日本官方机构已发起针对他们的运动，并报道称，如果维持其给养对市政财政的消耗持续下去，日本纳税人可能会拒绝缴纳捐税。这是一个所罗门式的难题，可以 assured 那些喧闹的日本纳税人，工部局比任何人都更渴望解决这一问题，但至今无人提出解决办法。引发这场喧闹的日本报纸也没有提出办法。这是工部局必须继续忍受的困难之一，直到和平再次降临这个国家。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS
MAR 1 4 1939

“Lone Battalion”
Support
Chinese Financial Aid
Withdrawn; Council to
Assist Temporarily

The famous Chinese “Lone Bat-
talion,” whose valiant stand against
overwhelming Japanese forces in the
Joint Savings Bank godown on
North Soochow Road in November
1937, drew forth praise from all
over the world, are once again in the
news. It was revealed yesterday
that the various Chinese philanthropic
institutions, which had provided the
funds necessary for the maintenance
of the soldiers at the internment
camp near Kiaochow Park, since they
fled from the godown into the
Settlement, had withdrawn that sup-
port owing to financial difficulties.
The “North-China Daily News” was
informed by a high official of the
Shanghai Municipal Council yester-
day that for the past two months the
cost of maintaining the 370 soldiers
had been borne by the Council,
although every effort was being
made to transfer that cost to other
bodies. This, he explained, was
being arranged by the Chinese
members of the Council, who would
report on what had been accom-
plished in the near future.
Asked what action would be taken
if the necessary financial support
was not forthcoming, the official
stated that this was a hypothetical
question although he did not think
that the soldiers would be released.
Although no information was given
as to the cost of maintaining the
interned battalion, a report from a
reliable source yesterday stated that
about $4,500 were being spent each
month by the S.M.C. in this con-
nection.
The “Lone Battalion” is commanded
by Col. Hsieh Chin-yuan and Major
Yang Jui-fu, graduates of the
Whampoa Military Academy, both
these officers being interned with
their men after their retreat from
the godown into the Settlement,
where they were disarmed by British
soldiers and taken to the Kiaochow
Road internment camp.
It will be recalled that in August
of last year members of the battalion
rioted over the question of the rais-
ing of the Chinese national flag in
the camp to mark the anniversary of
the commencement of the fighting in
Shanghai. Four of the soldiers were
killed during a sanguinary battle
with Russian volunteers and sixteen
were injured before the riot was
subdued.

（右上角批注：POLICE REGISTRY 8037/1.31 14 3 3）
pages.zh:
《字林西报》
1939年3月14日

“孤军”
支援
中国财政援助
撤回；工部局将
暂时协助

著名的中国“孤军”因1937年11月在苏州河北岸的四行联合储蓄仓库面对压倒性优势的日军进行的英勇抵抗而赢得全世界的赞誉，如今再次成为新闻焦点。昨日披露，自士兵们从仓库逃入租界以来，一直为胶州公园附近拘禁营内的士兵提供必要维持资金的各中国慈善机构，因财政困难已撤回支持。

《字林西报》昨日从上海公共租界工部局的一位高级官员处获悉，过去两个月维持这370名士兵的费用已由工部局承担，尽管各方正努力将这笔费用转移给其他机构。他解释说，此事正由工部局华董安排，他们将在不久的将来报告进展情况。

当被问及如果必要的财政支持不到位将采取何种行动时，该官员表示这是一个假设性问题，尽管他认为士兵们不会被释放。

虽然没有提供维持被拘禁团体的费用信息，但昨日来自可靠消息源的报告称，上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）每月在此方面的支出约为4,500美元。

“孤军”由谢晋元上校和杨瑞符少校指挥，两人均为黄埔军校毕业生。这两名军官在从仓库撤退到租界后，与他们的部下一起被拘禁，在那里他们被英军解除武装，并被带往胶州路拘禁营。

回想去年八月，该团成员曾因在营内升起中国国旗以纪念上海战斗开始周年纪念日的问题而发生骚乱。在与俄国志愿人员的一场血腥战斗中，四名士兵丧生，十六人受伤，随后骚乱才被平息。

（右上角批注：警务登记处 8037/1.31 14 3 3）

CHINA DAILY NEWS
FEB 22 1939
5039 A/Bf 3
24 2 39

Inmate Disappears from
Lone Battalion Camp

Mystery Unsolved as Way
Of Escape Unknown

Private Shao Kung-Ky, 22, one
of the inmates of the Lone Battalion,
interned at a special camp off Kaochow
Road on Singapore Road, mysteriously
disappeared, during the night from Monday to yesterday, his
absence being discovered yesterday
morning at the usual roll call. A
search throughout the camp was
immediately commenced but no trace
of him could be found. It was
furthermore established that he definitely did not pass any of the many
entries of the Russian Regiment,
Shanghai Volunteer Corps which
surround the camp.

Detectives from Gordon Road station which were called in to solve
the mystery were puzzled, as the
camp is believed to be escape-proof
and as it was reasoned that if he
was able to make his escape over
the eight foot wall surrounding the
camp, which has barbed wire on the
top, at least traces of blood or rent
in his clothing would have been
found, and this was not the case.
A close scrutiny of the barbed
wire, revealed not the slightest clue
as to how he may have passed over
it at all.

One of the places where he might
have landed, if it seems to be the
case he managed to make his escape
over the wall, was the Kiaochow Road
Park; but the watchmen on duty there
said that they had seen nothing.
Meanwhile police stations in the
Settlement and the Concession have
all been given a description of the
fugitive and are on the lookout for him,
but it is doubtful as to whether he
will ever be found. It seems likely that
he will find safe refuge practically in
any Chinese home, as members of
the Battalion are considered national
heroes, after their siege in a Chinese
temple down Chapei area, Soochow
Creek.

Last summer considerable difficulties were experienced in keeping the
inmates of the camp under the strict
discipline imposed on them and, over
the question of flying the Chinese
national flag on the anniversary of
the outbreak of local hostilities, a
fight ensued between the inmates and
the Russian soldiers, resulting in a
number of them being injured.
About two or three died of their
wounds.

1939年2月22日
5039 A/Bf 3
39年2月24日

孤军营一名在押人员失踪

逃脱方式不明，谜团未解

邵公基（Shao Kung-Ky，音译）下士，22岁，系被拘禁于新加坡路高州路附近特种营房内的“孤军”在押人员之一，于周一至昨日的夜间神秘失踪，其缺席情况于昨日早晨例行点名时被发现。随即在营内展开搜查，但未发现其任何踪迹。此外已查明，他确实未经过包围该营房的上海义勇队俄国团（Russian Regiment, Shanghai Volunteer Corps）的众多入口中的任何一处。

戈登路捕房奉命介入以解开此谜团的侦探们感到困惑，因为该营房被认为无法逃脱，且据推断，如果他能够翻越周围八英尺高、顶部装有铁丝网的围墙，至少会发现血迹或其衣物上的撕裂痕迹，但事实并非如此。对铁丝网进行的仔细检查，并未显示出丝毫关于他如何翻越过去的线索。

如果确如推测他是翻墙逃脱，他可能落地的地点之一是胶州路公园；但那里的值班看守表示他们什么也没看见。与此同时，租界和法租界的各警察分局均已收到该逃犯的特征描述并正在留意搜寻，但他能否被找到尚存疑问。看来他很可能会在几乎任何中国家庭中找到安全的庇护所，因为在闸北地区苏州河畔的一座中国庙宇中被围困后，“孤军”成员被视为民族英雄。

去年夏天，在对营内在押人员实施严格纪律方面遇到了相当大的困难，而且，就在当地战事爆发周年纪念日悬挂中国国旗的问题上，在押人员与俄国士兵之间发生了斗殴，导致多人受伤。其中约两三人因伤死亡。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

JAN 1 1939

LONE BATTALION TO
LOSE COMMANDER

Colonel Hsieh Will Go
To Hospital; Suffers
From Severe Chill

Colonel Hsieh Chung yuan of the
interned "Lone Battalion" here, has
entered a hospital for a prolonged
rest and will probably spend the
winter there, it was learnt yesterday.

The "Lone Battalion," it may be
recalled, became world-famous in
the later part of October, 1937,
when they staged a daring stand at
the Joint Savings godown against
the Japanese. Only after having
received orders from the highest
military authorities of the Chinese
Government did the battalion retreat into the Settlement areas.

Since then, the troops, amounting
to 350, have been living in a concentration camp located on Singapore Road under the guardianship
of Russian members of the S V C.

A visit to the camp reveals that
Colonel Hsieh and his subordinates,
whom he calls "brothers," are leading normal civil lives. The
"brothers" are fond of playing
basketball, while the colonel himself enjoys a game of tennis once
in a while. Life at the camp begins
at 5 a m and ends at 8 p.m.

（批：D- 2/1）

《上海泰晤士报》

1939年1月1日

孤军将失去指挥官

谢团长将入院；患严重寒症

据悉，昨日，此处被拘禁的“孤军”团长谢晋元（Hsieh Chung yuan，音译）已入院进行长期休养，并可能在那里度过整个冬季。

回想起来，“孤军”在1937年10月下旬因在四行仓库对日军进行大胆抵抗而举世闻名。该团仅在接到中国政府最高军事当局的命令后，才撤退进入租界区域。

此后，这支共计350人的部队一直生活在位于新加坡路的集中营内，由上海义勇队（S V C）的俄国成员负责看守。

走访该营房显示，谢团长及其被他称为“兄弟”的部下过着正常的平民生活。“兄弟们”喜爱打篮球，而谢团长本人则偶尔享受打网球的乐趣。营房生活从上午5点开始，至晚上8点结束。

（批注：D- 2/1）

SHANGHAI TIMES,

NOV 20 1938

COUNCIL ASKED FOR
AN INVESTIGATION

Another Camp Incident
Reported With Pupil
As New “Victim”

The Chinese Ratepayers' Association of the International Settlement has forwarded an official letter to the Shanghai Municipal Council requesting that investigations be made into the alleged manhandling of a Chinese school-boy by the Russian watchman of the Kiaochow Road camp of the "Lone Battalion," which incident has been given prominence by the Chinese press.

Referring to the former incident in which several members of the battalion suffered injuries in a clash with the Russian volunteer on guard at the camp, the letter complained about the repeated "rough action" on the part of the Russian guards and requested the Council to investigate and to punish the Russian guard involved in the latest incident.

The incident was reported to have taken place on Wednesday, shortly after 5 p.m., when a party of Chinese students was about to leave the camp under the leadership of an American teacher. One of the youths wished to leave the camp earlier than his companions and accompanied by a Chinese soldier living in the camp he went to the camp door but due to some misunderstanding, of which no explanation has been given, a Russian guard is alleged to have beaten the boy. Colonel Hsieh, commander of the battalion, has brought the matter to the attention of the Council authorities. The students went to the camp in order to play some games with the interned soldiers.

《上海泰晤士报》，

1938年11月20日

要求理事会进行调查

另一起营房事件被报道，学生成为新“受害者”

公共租界华人纳税会已向上海公共租界工部局递交正式信函，要求对所谓“孤军”胶州路营房的俄国看守殴打一名中国男学生的事件进行调查，该事件已受到中文报刊的重点关注。

信中提及此前发生的数名单兵在与营房执勤的俄国志愿兵冲突中受伤的事件，抱怨俄国看守反复采取“粗暴行动”，并要求理事会调查并惩处卷入最新事件的俄国看守。

据报道，该事件发生于周三下午5点后不久，当时一群中国学生在一位美国教师的带领下正准备离开营房。其中一名青年希望比同伴更早离开，并由一名居住在营房内的中国士兵陪同前往营门，但由于某种尚未解释的误会，据称一名俄国看守殴打了该男孩。“孤军”指挥官谢团长已将此事提请理事会当局注意。学生们前往营房是为了与被拘禁的士兵进行一些游戏活动。

CHINA PRESS.

NOV 19 1938

‘Lone Battalion’
IncidentProtest
Still Unreplied

Gonzaga College Pupil
Said Maltreated By
Russian Guard

Representations made to the
Shanghai Municipal Council against
the alleged attack by a Russian
guard at the “Lone Battalion” con-
centration camp on a pupil of
Gonzaga College last Wednesday,
have not yet been replied. THE
CHINA PRESS learned yesterday.
The schoolboy, named Tan Wei-
chiu, who was reportedly punched
on the head by the guard, was
well and attended school as usual
yesterday, it was further learned.
The incident allegedly occurred
last Wednesday afternoon when a
party of pupils of Gonzaga College,
734 Kiaochow Road, led by a for-
eign teacher, visited the “Lone
Battalion” concentration camp
situated on the same road to com-
fort the interned Chinese troops.
Everything went on smoothly
until the time the pupils were leav-
ing the camp for home at 5:15 p.m.
It appeared that one of the stu-
dents, by the name of Tan, wanted
to go first and was accompanied to
the entrance by one of the interned
soldiers.
A Russian guard, allegedly dis-
pleased by the boy’s departure, was
said to have manhandled him, re-
sulting in the slight injury of the
latter.
It was asserted yesterday that
the reason for the attack was that
the student did not shut the door
as he left—which was later shut by
the soldier who accompanied him.
THE CHINA PRESS learned yester-
day that shortly afterward both
officials of the “Lone Battalion” and
the Gonzaga College separately
lodged protests with the Shanghai
Municipal Council in connection
with the incident.

Like
C.C.

《大美晚报》

1938年11月19日

“孤军”事件抗议
仍未获回复

据称公教学校学生
遭俄国看守虐待

《大美晚报》昨日获悉，针对上周三一名公教学校（Gonzaga College，音译）学生在“孤军”集中营 alleged 遭受俄国看守袭击一事向上海公共租界工部局提出的交涉，尚未得到回复。进一步获悉，这名 reportedly 被看守击打头部的名叫谭维秋（Tan Wei-chiu，音译）的男学生身体状况良好，昨日照常上学。

据称，该事件发生于上周三下午，当时公教学校（地址：胶州路734号）的一群学生在一位外籍教师的带领下，访问了位于同一条路上的“孤军”集中营，以慰问被拘禁的中国军队。

一切进展顺利，直到下午5点15分学生们准备离开营房回家时。似乎是一名姓谭的学生想先走，并由一名被拘禁士兵陪同至入口处。

据称，一名俄国看守因对该男孩的离去感到不满，对其进行了粗暴对待，导致后者轻微受伤。

昨日有人声称，袭击的原因是该学生离开时未关门——后来由陪同他的士兵关上了门。《大美晚报》昨日获悉，此后不久，“孤军”官员和公教学校分别就此事向上海公共租界工部局提出了抗议。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

NOV 4 1938

Proclamation Made
By Col. Hsieh

Colonel Hsieh Ching-yuan,
Commander of the famous
'Lost Battalion" now interned
in Shanghai, has issued a pro-
clamation to the people of
China on the occasion of the
first anniversary of the battle
at the Joint Savings Godown.
Colonel Hsieh stated that he
was a great advocate of the
scorched earth policy but that
he and his men were full of
regret that they couldn't be at
the front.
The commander also ex-
pressed his gratitude for the
deep concern shown by the
general public over the wel-
fare of his men. In con-
clusion, he said that the
troubles of China would

CHINA PRESS.
OCT 27 1930
The “Sympathy Grant”

Editor, THE CHINA PRESS
Sir,—The clash between the Chinese soldiers and Russian Volunteers on August 11 has for the past two months aroused the attention of the local community. The Chinese residents of Shanghai have openly expressed dissatisfaction and resentment toward the Shanghai Municipal Council for handling the incident in a rather high-handed way. Following the return of the Chinese National Flag on August 21, friendly negotiations with the S.M.C. finally made possible an amicable settlement of the case as revealed in a letter of the S.M.C. to the C.R.A. which reads in part as follows:

“On humanitarian grounds the Council has decided to grant the sum of $1,000 to the dependents of each of the men who died of injuries. Accordingly I have pleasure in enclosing a cheque for $3,000, with the request that your Association ascertain the names and addresses of the dependents properly entitled to the money, and hand it over to them.”

All went well when fresh trouble started by two letters in the correspondence column of a morning paper of this city. (October 12 and 14). The authors of the letters evidently meant to find fault or make trouble with the S.M.C. when they protested against the decision of the Council and complained childishly about the “sympathy grant” of $3,000 Chinese currency. What greatly surprised me was the immediate response and editorial support of the North-China Daily News. In the issue of the British journal for October 14 I discovered an editorial on the “Mistaken Policy” of the S.M.C. in which the Council’s letter was characterized as “abject in its terms, overflowing with regrets and expressions of sympathy,—a very humble communication.” It went on to ask “many interesting questions” in regard to the decision of the Council. In short, the leading editorial ought to convince its readers that the S.M.C. could and should have saved those $3,000 and let the Chinese soldiers (and their dependents) go to the devil. On the editorial and the letters in question I have commented rather bluntly in a letter to the China Critic in its issue for October 20. But here I wish to point out that the North-China Daily News has by so doing vindicated itself, at least for once against current charges of its pro-S.M.C. attitude and policy.

That the editor of the N.-C. D. N. expressed his convictions on the basis of inadequate information was clearly borne out by an article in THE CHINA PRESS for October 15 in which spokesmen of the S.M.C. deplored the wrong attitude and hasty judgment of certain critics against the reasonable settlement of the Lone Battalion case. At the risk of repetition let me quote a few passages from the said article.

1. “It has been said of the Council that, in granting $1,000 to each of the three men who died of injuries received in the affray, has placed a premium on lawlessness by paying compensation to the relatives of men whose deaths were the direct cause of the fight, thus encouraging further disorders. . . . Far from rewarding lawlessness, the S.M.C. merely granted the minimum compensation to the dependents of the deceased soldiers.

2. “There was nothing more important than that harmonious relations between the S.M.C. and the Chinese community should be maintained. It is the duty of the Council to attempt to maintain good relations not only with the Chinese, but also with all other national groups in this cosmopolitan city.

3. “The incident unfortunately involved the Chinese National Flag and in dealing with the situation, the Council had to take into account Chinese patriotic feelings, their psychology and their point of view.

4. “The Russian Regiment was sent primarily to enforce discipline, and it was not expected that violence and fatal injuries would result. It was only natural that the Council should seek to make retribution when enforcement of discipline resulted inadvertently in deaths. . . . The money was handed over to the Chinese Ratepayers Association, and if dependents cannot be found, the money will be returned to the Council.

3. “There is not a single argument which will convince the Chinese community that the interned soldiers should not have flown their National Flag on August 13, the anniversary of the outbreak of hostilities here.”

The mis-guided judgment of the N.-C. D. N. was further exposed by an editorial in the Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury on the “Sympathy Grant.” Permit me to quote from the editorial for your reader’s reference.

《字林西报》。
1930年10月27日
“抚恤金”

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

8月11日中国士兵与俄国志愿人员之间的冲突，在过去两个月里引起了本地社会的关注。上海中国居民公开表达了对工部局以相当强硬的方式处理此事的不满和愤慨。随着8月21日中国国旗的归还，通过与工部局的友好谈判，最终使此案得以和解，这一点在工部局致华人纳税会的一封信中有所披露，该信部分内容如下：

“出于人道主义理由，本董事会决定向每名因伤致死者的家属发放1,000美元。因此，我谨随函附上3,000美元的支票一张，并请贵会查明有权领取该款项的家属姓名及地址，并将款项转交予他们。”

一切本来进展顺利，直到本市一家晨报的读者来信栏刊登了两封信（10月12日和14日），引发了新的麻烦。这两封信的作者显然意在挑剔或给工部局制造麻烦，他们抗议董事会的决定，并幼稚地抱怨这笔3,000元法币的“抚恤金”。令我大为惊讶的是，《字林西报》立即作出回应并在社论中予以支持。在该英资报刊10月14日的版面上，我发现了一篇关于工部局“错误政策”的社论，其中将董事会的信形容为“措辞卑躬屈膝，充满了遗憾和同情的表达——一封非常谦卑的信函”。接着，该社论就董事会的决定提出了“许多有趣的问题”。简而言之，这篇头版社论旨在让读者相信，工部局能够且应该省下这3,000美元，让那些中国士兵（及其家属）见鬼去。针对该社论及相关信件，我在10月20日出版的《中国评论周报》上发表了一封信，进行了相当直率的评论。但在此我想指出，《字林西报》通过此举至少在一次事件中洗刷了自身，反驳了当前对其持亲工部局态度和政策的指控。

《字林西报》编辑基于不充分的信息表达其观点，这一事实由10月15日《字林西报》上的一篇文章清楚地证实，文中工部局发言人对某些批评家对“孤军营”案件合理和解所持的错误态度和草率判断表示惋惜。冒着重复之嫌，请允许我从该文章中引用几段文字。

1. “有人指责董事会，称其向在冲突中受伤致死的三人每人发放1,000美元，是通过向死者亲属支付赔偿金来奖励违法行为，因为他们的死亡是引发战斗的直接原因，从而鼓励进一步的骚乱……工部局绝非奖励违法行径，仅仅是向阵亡士兵的家属提供了最低限度的补偿。

2. “没有什么比维持工部局与中国社区之间的和谐关系更重要。董事会有责任不仅努力维持与华人的良好关系，也要维持与这座国际都市中所有其他国籍群体的良好关系。

3. “不幸的是，此事件涉及中国国旗，在处理局势时，董事会必须考虑到中国人的爱国情感、他们的心理以及他们的观点。

4. “派遣俄兵团主要是为了执行纪律，并未预料到会导致暴力和致命伤害。当执行纪律不慎导致死亡时，董事会寻求做出补救是自然而然的……这笔钱已交给华人纳税会，如果找不到家属，款项将退还给董事会。

3. “没有任何一个论点能说服中国社区，认为被拘禁的士兵不应在8月13日——即此地战事爆发周年纪念日——升起他们的国旗。”

《字林西报》受到误导的判断进一步被《上海晚邮报与水星报》关于“抚恤金”的一篇社论所揭露。请允许我引用该社论的部分内容，供读者参考。

“显然，我们的一些外国读者认为我们应该批评工部局。相反，我们认为，鉴于此次纠纷在中国社区引发的普遍情绪，工部局的做法是明智的。……无论如何，这一先例的核心在于，当发生了一起令各方都感到遗憾的不幸事件时，在试图解决此事时表现出慷慨是有理由的。
“在我们看来，工部局只是试图采取务实的态度，并为对此类事件的发生表示遗憾找到具体的表达方式。其支付的3,000美元是一种象征性的付款，一种东方式的妥协。如果工部局完全理亏，3,000美元是不够的赔偿。即使工部局完全占理，在这种情况下，为了抚慰受伤的感情而稍作让步，也颇符合远东的观念。
“切勿误解——中国社区的感情在此事中受到了伤害。‘孤军’被中国人奉为偶像，他们如今处境艰难，值得给予一定的体谅。这并不意味着应该无原则地向他们让步。但在这一国际社区中，让我们的中国成员感觉到他们并未因其军队撤离而受到压迫，这对任何人都没有害处。”
现在，得益于工部局和华人纳税会的合作以及众多外国同情者的支持，8月11日的“孤军”事件已得到友好解决。“孤军”通过斗争和流血成功捍卫了中国国旗，因为他们悬挂青天白日旗的权利得到了所有有识之士的无可争议的认可。正如一位中国通讯员所指出的那样（《字林西报》，10月15日），中国社区从工部局接收这3,000美元时，并非带着胜利的心态，而是怀着友好的感激之情。
“我这样说对吗？”
上海，1938年10月20日。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
OCT 1 7 1938

That “Sympathy Grant”

SEVERAL PEOPLE have inquired why we have
failed to comment on the Shanghai
Municipal Council’s “sympathy grant” of
$3000 to the families of three Chinese
soldiers of the interned “Lone Battalion” who
were killed during the recent disciplinary fracas
in their camp.

It is apparently felt by some of our foreign
readers that we should criticize the Council.
On the contrary we believe that in view of the
emotion prevalent in the Chinese community
as result of this trouble, the Council acted
wisely. Its actions were dictated by what may
be termed political considerations, but why
not? Its decision is assailed as setting a bad
precedent, but why? The Council is not a law
court, compelled to be bound rigidly by pre-
cedent, and in any event the essential part of
this precedent is that when there has been an
unfortunate occurrence regretted all around
there is some reason for manifesting generosity
in trying to settle the matter. Such a prece-
dent probably must be followed in its most
fundamental aspect if we have any more dif-
ficulty of comparable sort. In fact we believe
that this community is in general “hard boiled”
to a degree incredible elsewhere on compen-
sation matters, and a little thinking on the
subject may do none of us any harm.

Regard the whole affair realistically. Both
the soldiers and the Council authorities were
to blame, it seems to us, in letting the intern-
ment camp ferment into a state where such a
serious clash occurred. There was evidently a
lack of employment for the men and a lack of
understanding on both sides. Finally a lot of
mercenaries of another nationality from either
of the chiefly interested parties waded in,
under orders, and three fatalities among the
interned men were the result, along with a
lot of other casualties. That was bad business
whatever its cause. Our local Chinese com-
munity, which pays a very large share of the
rates, became extremely concerned and per-
haps unjustifiably exercised against the Coun-
cil’s eventual severity. It all added up to a
mess where examination into the initial details
became of no use.

As we see it, the Council merely tried to
be practical and to find concrete expression (at
no very great cost, either) of a regret that any
such thing happened. Its $3000 was a sort of
token payment, an Orient compromise. Had
the Council been completely in the wrong,
$3000 would not have been enough payment.
Had the Council been completely in the right
even then it accords pretty well with Far East
ideas to yield slightly in the interest of salving
hurt feelings.

And make no mistake—the feelings of the
Chinese community were hurt by this affair.
The “Lone Battalion” has been idolized by the
Chinese, who are in a very difficult position
nowadays and who deserve some consideration.
That does not mean they should be given in
so unreasonably. But in this international
community it will harm nobody to let our Chin-
ese members feel they are not being oppressed
because of the withdrawal of their army.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》。
1938年10月17日

那笔“抚恤金”

有几位人士询问，为何我们没有评论上海公共租界工部局向近期在营内纪律纠纷中遇难的三名被拘禁“孤军”中国士兵家属发放的3,000美元“抚恤金”。

显然，我们的一些外国读者认为我们应该批评工部局。相反，我们认为，鉴于此次纠纷在中国社区引发的普遍情绪，工部局的做法是明智的。其行动是由可称为政治考量的因素所驱使，但这有何不可？其决定被抨击为树立了不良先例，但这又是为何？工部局并非法院，不受必须严格遵循先例的约束，而且无论如何，这一先例的核心在于，当发生了一起令各方都感到遗憾的不幸事件时，在试图解决此事时表现出慷慨是有理由的。如果我们将来再遇到类似性质的困难，这一先例在其最根本的方面可能必须得到遵循。事实上，我们认为，本社区在赔偿问题上总体上“冷酷无情”到了在其他地方令人难以置信的程度，对此事稍加思考对我们大家都无害处。

现实地看待整个事件。在我们看来，士兵和工部局当局都有责任，任由拘禁营发酵至发生如此严重冲突的状态。显然，士兵们缺乏工作，双方缺乏理解。最后，来自主要利益相关方之一的另一国籍的大量雇佣兵奉命介入，导致被拘禁人员中有三人死亡，以及其他许多伤亡。无论起因如何，这都是糟糕的事情。缴纳大部分捐税的本埠中国社区变得极度关切，并对工部局最终的严厉态度感到或许是不公正的愤怒。这一切汇总成一团乱麻，使得审查初始细节变得毫无用处。

在我们看来，工部局只是试图采取务实的态度，并以（代价也不大）具体的方式表达对发生此类事件的遗憾。其支付的3,000美元是一种象征性的付款，一种东方式的妥协。如果工部局完全理亏，3,000美元是不够的赔偿。即使工部局完全占理，在这种情况下，为了抚慰受伤的感情而稍作让步，也颇符合远东的观念。

切勿误解——中国社区的感情在此事中受到了伤害。“孤军”被中国人奉为偶像，他们如今处境艰难，值得给予一定的体谅。这并不意味着应该无原则地向他们让步。但在这一国际社区中，让我们的中国成员感觉到他们并未因其军队撤离而受到压迫，这对任何人都没有害处。

CHINA PRESS.
OCT 1 5 1938
Settlement Of Dispute
Over Interned Troops
Said Most Reasonable
S.M.C. Councillor And
Spokesman Defend
$3,000 Grant
DEPLORE CRITICS'
WRONG ATTITUDE
Necessity For Complete
Accord In Shanghai
Emphasized

All criticisms thus far directed against the Shanghai Municipal Council in connection with the settlement of the situation arising from the clash between the "Lone Battalion" and Russian Regiment on August 11 indicate a lack of knowledge of the facts of the case an S.M.C. councillor informed THE CHINA PRESS yesterday.
It has been said of the Council that, in granting $1,000 to each of the three men who died of injuries received in the affray, has placed a premium on lawlessness by paying compensation to the relatives of men whose deaths were the direct cause of the fight thus encouraging further disorders.
In making these grants, the Shanghai Municipal Council addressed a letter to the Chinese Ratepayers' Association, stating that "on humanitarian grounds the Council has decided to grant the sum of $1,000 to the dependents of each of the men who died of injuries."
To the letter was enclosed a check for $3,000, with the request that the association ascertain the names and addresses of the dependents properly entitled to the money, and hand it over to them.
Minimum Compensation
Far from rewarding lawlessness, the councillor continued, the S.M.C merely granted the minimum compensation to the dependents of the deceased soldiers. There was nothing more important, he said, than that harmonious relation between the S.M.C. and the Chinese community should be maintained.
It is the duty of the Council to attempt to maintain good relations not only with the Chinese but also with all other national groups in this cosmopolitan city.
Another Council spokesman told THE CHINA PRESS that the criticisms merely indicated that the critics viewed the incident from a completely wrong perspective. It was not merely a dispute between the "Lone Battalion" and those responsible for guarding the camp, but it had developed a feeling of resentment on the part of the entire Chinese community against the Council.
The critics also fail to understand, he added, that the incident unfortunately involved the Chinese National flag, and that in dealing with the situation the Council had to take into account Chinese patriotic feelings, their psychology and then general point of view.
Furthermore, it must be remembered, he said, that there are five Chinese councillors in the Settlement administration upon whom the Chinese community undeniably exercised pressure.
What started as a minor row developed a political aspect, and it was imperative that the matter be settled amicably in the best way possible. Furthermore, it was pointed out that the Russian Regiment was sent primarily to enforce discipline, and it was not expected that violence and fatal injuries would result. It was only natural, he felt, that the Council should seek to make restitution when enforcement of discipline resulted inadvertently in deaths.
There is not a single argument which will convince the Chinese community that the interned should not have flown their National Flag on August 17, the anniversary of the outbreak of hostilities here. It would have been just as hard for any other patriotic community under the same circumstances, to understand it, it was pointed out.
Dependents Real Sufferers
It was also pointed out that the real sufferers of the future are not the deceased soldiers, but their dependents. The Council acted in the belief that each man had dependents, for the family system in China is such that even distant aged relatives quite naturally depend upon young men for support. The money was handed over, to the Chinese Ratepayers Association, a reputable body. The logical of this procedure is that, if dependents cannot be found the money will be returned to the Council.

1938年10月15日

就拘禁士兵争端达成和解
据称最为合理
工部局董事及发言人
为3,000美元拨款辩护
痛惜批评者态度错误
强调上海亟需完全和谐

工部局一名董事昨日向《字林西报》表示，迄今为止针对上海公共租界工部局在处理8月11日“孤军”与俄兵团冲突所引发局势方面的所有批评，均表明批评者缺乏对案件事实的了解。
有人指责工部局向在斗殴中受伤致死的三人每人发放1,000美元，是通过向死者家属支付赔偿金来奖励不法行为，因为死者的死亡是引发战斗的直接原因，从而鼓励了进一步的骚乱。
在发放这笔款项时，上海公共租界工部局致函华人纳税会，声明“出于人道主义理由，本局决定向每名因伤致死者的受扶养人发放1,000美元”。
随信附有一张3,000美元的支票，并请该会查明有权获得此款项的受扶养人的姓名和地址，并将款项转交给他们。

最低限度赔偿
该董事继续说道，工部局此举绝非奖励不法行为，而仅仅是向已故士兵的受扶养人提供了最低限度的赔偿。他说，没有什么比维持工部局与华人社区之间的和谐关系更为重要的了。
工部局有责任不仅努力维持与华人的良好关系，也要维持与这座国际性都市中所有其他国籍群体的良好关系。
另一位工部局发言人对《字林西报》表示，这些批评仅仅表明批评者从完全错误的角度看待这一事件。这不仅仅是“孤军”与负责看守营地的人员之间的纠纷，而且已在整个华人社区中引发了对工部局的怨恨情绪。
他补充说，批评者也未能理解，不幸的是，这一事件涉及中国国旗，工部局在处理该局势时必须考虑到中国人的爱国情感、他们的心理以及一般的观点。
此外，他说，必须记住，租界行政机构中有五名华人董事，华人社区无疑对他们施加了压力。
起初只是一场小争执，后来发展出了政治层面，因此必须以尽可能最好的方式和平解决此事，这一点至关重要。此外，有人指出，派遣俄兵团主要是为了执行纪律，并未预料到会导致暴力和致命伤害。他认为，当执行纪律无意中导致死亡时，工部局寻求做出补偿是自然而然的。
没有任何一种论点能说服华人社区相信，被拘禁者不应在8月17日悬挂他们的国旗，那天是此地战事爆发的周年纪念日。有人指出，任何其他具有爱国精神的社区在相同情况下，也会同样难以理解这一点。

受扶养人才是真正的受害者
还有人指出，未来真正的受害者不是已故士兵，而是他们的受扶养人。工部局基于每个人都拥有受扶养人的信念采取行动，因为中国的家庭制度使得即使是远亲中的年老亲属也很自然地依赖年轻人供养。这笔钱交给了声誉良好的华人纳税会。这一程序的逻辑在于，如果找不到受扶养人，款项将退还给工部局。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

OCT 1 5 1938

"Mistaken Policy":
A Chinese Point of View
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,--That the Chinese soldiers
interned in Kiaochow Park might
have been difficult to control
was likely. But that the punishment
inflicted upon them of having three
men beaten to death and more than
twenty others severely wounded was
a bit too harsh could not be denied.
If the matter had been skilfully
handled it might not have had such
unfortunate results. It is only right
that the incident should now be
closed by an amicable settlement.
Had this amicable settlement not
been reached, the Camp Commandant
and the interned soldiers would
still regard each other with suspicion
and this suspicion might well be the
cause of worse troubles in future.
Your editorial was right in saying
that discipline cannot be bought.
Discipline has not been bought in
this case.
I cannot agree that the letter
addressed by the Acting Secretary
of the Municipal Council to the
Chinese Ratepayers' Association is a
"very humble communication" as I
am sure that the Association would
receive it with gratitude and a
feeling of friendly appreciation
rather than of triumph. The request
made when the $3,000 were handed
to the Chinese Ratepayers' Associa-
tion that the Association should
ascertain the names and addresses
of the dependents properly entitled
to the money and hand it over to
them in my opinion was sufficient.
If the Council think that they can
trust the distribution of the com-
pensation to another public body of
repute it need not go into the trouble
of ascertaining the names and
addresses of the dependents itself.
The Council has done its duty.
Let us not assess the value of
human lives in the terms of how
many dollars each. There may be
people like DISGRACE and ONLOOKER
who think that the compensation of
$3,000 is not justifiable. But there
are plenty others who having seen
the soldiers put up such a magni-
ficent defence of their country regard
them as noble creatures whose lives
cannot be compensated by pecuniary
rewards.
The hypothesis put forward by
your Editor in the last paragraph of
his editorial was admitted by him-
self to be ridiculous and certainly
cannot be compared with this case.
So why mention it.
N. L. L.
Shanghai, Oct. 14.

“错误的政策”：
一个中国人的观点
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生——被拘禁在胶州公园（Kiaochow Park）的中国士兵可能难以控制，这是有可能的。但是，不可否认，对他们施加的惩罚——三人被殴打致死，二十多人受重伤——未免过于严厉。如果处理得当，或许不会造成如此不幸的后果。现在通过友好和解来了结此事，是完全正确的。如果没有达成这种友好和解，营地指挥官和被拘禁士兵之间仍会相互猜疑，而这种猜疑很可能成为未来更严重麻烦的根源。
贵报社论说得对，纪律是不能靠金钱买来的。在此案中，纪律并没有被收买。
我不同意工部局代理秘书致华人纳税会的信函是一种“非常卑微的通函”的说法，因为我确信该会以感激和友好赞赏的心情，而非以胜利者的心态接收此信。在我看来，在将3,000美元交给华人纳税会时，要求该会查明有权获得此款项的受扶养人的姓名和地址并转交给他们，这一要求已经足够。如果工部局认为可以将赔偿金的分派工作委托给另一个享有声誉的公共团体，它就不必亲自去查明受扶养人的姓名和地址。工部局已经履行了其职责。
让我们不要用每人值多少美元来衡量生命的价值。也许像“可耻之徒”（DISGRACE）和“旁观者”（ONLOOKER）这样的人认为3,000美元的赔偿金是不合理的。但也有许多人看到士兵们如此英勇地保卫国家，视他们为高尚的人，其生命是无法用金钱补偿的。
贵报编辑在社论最后一段提出的假设，他自己也承认是荒谬的，当然不能与本案相提并论。那么何必提及呢。

N. L. L.
上海，10月14日。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

OCT 1 4 1938

MISTAKEN POLICY

The Municipal Council should feel by no means surprised if the manner in which they have dealt with the riot of the Chinese soldiers interned in Kiaochow Park is very severely criticised, for upon the closest scrutiny it is impossible to discover what principles of good government can possibly be invoked in its justification. Cutting away all the drapery which have been woven around the men involved, the facts are that they were interned during the course of hostilities around Shanghai, in accordance with the neutrality of the International Settlement, they had for months behaved in such a manner, that the Council itself had to confess that "It has been found recently by the Camp Commandant that it was becoming increasingly difficult, and at times impossible, to enforce any kind of discipline in the camp. Attempts to enforce discipline were met with obstruction, etc." and eventually these men flouted authority and created a riot in the suppression of which some of them were injured, three fatally. The matter was taken up by the Chinese Ratepayers Association, for what reason apart from sentiment it is impossible to understand, and the Council has decided to award compensation to the families of the dead men. The letter conveying this decision is abject in its terms, overflowing with regrets and expressions of sympathy,—a very humble communication. The only possible sentiment that could in the circumstances have been expressed would, surely, have been that the Council regretted that the behaviour of the men obliged its officers to take the action they did, for any modification of that point of view derogates from the authority of the Council and its servants. There should most certainly have been left no opening for any suggestion that the action of the officials concerned in any way deserved less than the completest support from the Council.

The communication to the Chinese Rate-payers Association continues:

On humanitarian grounds the Council has decided to grant the sum of $1,000 to the dependents of each of the men who died of injuries. Accordingly I have pleasure in enclosing a cheque for $3,000, with the request that your Association ascertain the names and addresses of the dependents properly entitled to the money, and hand it over to them.

Many interesting questions arise from the above passage. Have the Council been completely informed as to the number and nature of the dependents of the dead men? Have they any tangible evidence that any such people do in fact exist, and the closeness of their relationship with the three deceased? The answer implied above seems to be in the negative, for the Council asks the Association to "ascertain the names and addresses of the dependents properly entitled to the money, and hand it over to them." Three thousand dollars have been handed over to the Association, a most reputable organization it is readily admitted, for it to pass on to people who apparently from the available evidence have made no claims, and whose identities are at present unknown to the Council, or even to the Association which is requested to discover them. The Municipal Council cannot possibly believe that many ratepayers will readily accept this arrangement as a business-like settlement of the trouble. Admitting that the reason for this grant is purely humanitarian, was it really necessary that the Council should make it without itself being certain that there are dependents who have suffered by the deaths of these men? On the face of the Acting Secretary's letter no such case has been made out, and, even if it were, it is open to very considerable doubt whether this is a proper instance in which such compensation should have been granted, for the men obviously suffered as a result of their own disorderly behaviour.

It must be obvious to everyone that this affair establishes an unfortunate precedent, one which verges on the absurd, and if at some future date the Council finds itself faced with a demand from the relatives of an armed robber, shot while fighting the police, there will be many who will fail to perceive very much real difference between the two cases. Certainly the hypothetical instance is ridiculous, and this settlement very little removed from it. Nor will the Shanghai public be at all impressed if at some time or other it is suggested that some esoteric doctrine of high policy is responsible for this extraordinary grant having been made. No matter what humanitarian gloss may be spread over this settlement, it has the unhappy appearance of an agreement made for the purpose of bringing about "harmonious relations......between the Council's officers responsible for guarding the camp and the interned officers and men." In other words a capitulation to the disorderly elements whose misbehaviour over a number of months culminated in a riot. There should be no very great surprise if it is ultimately shown that this magnanimous gesture on the part of the Council fails of its purpose. Discipline cannot be bought, and if this journal's reading of the facts is correct that is all that is being attempted. From the ratepayers' point of view a procedure which provides for the payment of compensation for losses to rioters or their dependents has nothing to commend it, for it must be quite clear that it merely serves to put a premium upon disorder. Obviously nothing can be done about it now, for whether for good or ill, the payment has been made and the matter, it is hoped, closed, but there can be nothing but regret that the policy which has been followed in this instance is most unfortunate, establishes a precedent which should never have been created, and must leave a sense of insecurity amongst those officials entrusted with the maintenance of law and order.

《字林西报》，

1938年10月14日

错误的政策

如果工部局处理胶州公园内被拘禁中国士兵骚乱的方式受到严厉批评，他们绝不应感到惊讶，因为经过最仔细的审查，人们无法找出任何可以为其辩护的良好治理原则。剥去围绕涉事人员编织的所有掩饰，事实是：在上海周边敌对行动期间，根据国际租界的中立地位，这些人被拘禁；数月来，他们的行为举止使得工部局不得不承认：“营地指挥官最近发现，在营地内执行任何纪律变得越来越困难，有时甚至不可能。试图执行纪律时遭到阻挠等。”最终，这些人蔑视权威并引发骚乱，在镇压过程中，其中一些人受伤，三人死亡。此事由华人纳税会提出，除了情感因素外，人们无法理解其理由何在，而工部局已决定向死者家属发放赔偿金。传达这一决定的信函措辞卑躬屈膝，充满了遗憾和同情的表达——这是一封非常谦卑的信函。在这种情况下，唯一可能表达的立场无疑是：工部局遗憾这些人的行为迫使其官员采取相应行动，因为对该观点的任何修正都会损害工部局及其仆役的权威。绝对不应留下任何余地，让人暗示相关官员的行动不值得工部局给予最全面的支持。

致华人纳税会的信函继续写道：

出于人道主义理由，工部局决定向每名因伤致死者的受扶养人发放1,000美元。因此，我随函附上3,000美元的支票一张，并请贵会查明有权领取该款项的受扶养人的姓名和地址，并将款项转交给他们。

上述段落引出了许多有趣的问题。工部局是否已完全了解死者的受扶养人的人数和性质？他们是否有任何确凿证据证明这些人确实存在，以及他们与三名死者关系的亲疏程度？上文隐含的答案似乎是否定的，因为工部局要求该协会“查明有权领取该款项的受扶养人的姓名和地址，并将款项转交给他们”。3,000美元已交给该协会——诚然，这是一个声誉极佳的机构——由其转交给那些根据现有证据显然并未提出索赔、且其身份目前连工部局甚至被要求查找他们的协会都一无所知的人。工部局不可能相信许多纳税人会轻易接受这种安排作为对此次事件的务实解决。即便承认这笔拨款纯粹是出于人道主义，工部局在自身不确定是否有受扶养人因这些人的死亡而遭受损失的情况下就进行拨款，这真的有必要吗？从代理秘书的信函表面来看，并未提出此类情况，而且即使提出了，在这种补偿是否应当发放的问题上也存在极大的疑问，因为这些人的遭遇显然是由其自身的无序行为造成的。

对每个人来说显而易见的是，此事确立了一个不幸的先例，一个近乎荒谬的先例。如果在未来的某个日期，工部局面临一名在与警察搏斗时被击毙的武装抢劫犯亲属提出的索赔要求，许多人将看不出这两起案件之间有什么真正的区别。当然，假设的例子是荒谬的，而这次和解与之相差无几。如果在任何时候有人暗示某种高深莫测的高层政策理论导致了这笔非凡拨款的发放，上海公众也不会对此留下任何印象。无论在这项和解之上涂抹何种人道主义的光泽，它都呈现出一种不幸的外观，即这项协议旨在促成“负责守卫营地的工部局官员与被拘禁的军官和士兵之间的‘和谐关系’……”。换句话说，这是对无序分子的投降，这些人在数月内的不当行为最终以骚乱告终。如果最终证明工部局的这一慷慨姿态未能达到其目的，也不必过于惊讶。纪律是无法购买的，如果本报对事实的解读正确，那么这正是目前所尝试的一切。从纳税人的角度来看，规定向暴乱者或其受扶养人支付损失赔偿的程序毫无可取之处，因为很明显，这只会助长无序行为。显然，现在对此已无能为力，因为无论好坏，款项已经支付，希望此事就此了结，但对于在此事中遵循的政策极其不幸、确立了一个本不该创造的先例，并必然在给受托维护法律和秩序的官员中留下不安全感这一点，只能表示遗憾。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
OCT 1 4 1938
The Camp Riot:
Some Pertinent Questions
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR, Your correspondent DISGRACE in today's issue is not alone in his view concerning the compensation paid out by the Shanghai Municipal Council. One small group of people I heard discussing the question were of the same opinion and it was remarked that "Someone is sure to write to the paper about it" although they each left for someone else to do.
Your correspondent asks: "Who pressed for payment for the dependents of the men killed? The question is a very natural one in view of the statement in the letter from the Council in which the Secretary states: "I have pleasure in enclosing a cheque for $3,000, with the request that your Association ascertain the names and addresses of the dependents properly entitled to the money and hand it over to them." Evidently the Council does not know to whom the money is to be paid and it is therefore apparent the pressure for compensation has not come from the dependents, as their names and addresses are not known to the Council. Why then should the money be handed over before this information is forthcoming and why has not the money been placed in some form of permanent security where it will be of lasting benefit to the dependents? What will become of the money should the Association fail in its efforts to discover the names and addresses of the dependents or whether there are any dependents at all. Will the money be returned to the Council? If the Council is to add this responsibility to its voluntary and humanitarian obligations, would it not be wise to at least commence at once to ascertain definitely the names and addresses of the dependents of the remaining members of the camp to whom payments could be made directly in future should another regrettable incident occur and whether they would like payment in cash or in kind, such as a memorial?
How did the Council arrive at the sum of $1,000 for compensation for each man killed? Is that the figure at which the Chinese Government assesses the value of human life? Have the dependents of men and women killed in times gone by been so compensated and are the dependents of men losing their lives in the present conflict being compensated anything like so generously, if at all?
If the Council had made any serious search for the Chinese Government's assessment of the value of human life it could have discovered it from the columns of the "North-China Daily News" which published a report from Canton dated April 16, reading as follows:
Railway Disaster Compensation.
Families of Deceased and Injured to be Given Cash.
Canton, Apr. 16
Measures for compensating the families of the victims of the fire which occurred on a train of the Canton-Kowloon Railway last Jan., have been communicated by the Ministry of Railways to the Kwangtung Provincial Government for enforcement.
According to these measures, $100 will be given to the family of each passenger killed, and $30 to each passenger injured. As there were 105 casualties, the total compensation will be $9,040.—Kuo Min.
It will be noted that the names and addresses of the families had apparently been ascertained and the payment made direct.
ONLOOKER.
Shanghai, Oct. 13

1938年10月14日
营地骚乱：
一些切中要害的问题
致《字林西报》编辑
先生，贵报今日刊登的署名“DISGRACE”的通讯员并非唯一对上海工部局支付的赔偿金持有看法的人。我听到一小群人在讨论这个问题，他们持相同意见，并评论说“肯定有人会写信给报纸谈论此事”，尽管每个人都指望别人去做。

贵报通讯员问道：“是谁为死者家属争取赔偿？”鉴于工部局信函中的声明，这是一个非常自然的问题，秘书在信中称：“我随函附上3,000美元的支票一张，并请贵会查明有权领取该款项的受扶养人的姓名和地址，并将款项转交给他们。”显然，工部局不知道钱要支付给谁，因此很明显，要求赔偿的压力并非来自受扶养人，因为工部局并不知道他们的姓名和地址。那么，为什么在这些信息尚未明确之前就要交出款项？为什么没有将款项以某种永久保障的形式存放，以便使受扶养人获得长久利益？如果协会未能查明受扶养人的姓名和地址，或者根本没有任何受扶养人，这笔钱将会怎样处理？钱会退还给工部局吗？如果工部局要将这一责任添加到其自愿和人道主义义务中，难道明智的做法不是至少立即开始确切查明营地其余成员的受扶养人的姓名和地址，以便将来若再次发生令人遗憾的事件时可以直接向他们付款，并询问他们是希望接受现金还是实物（如纪念碑）形式的支付？

工部局是如何得出每名死者赔偿1,000美元这一金额的？这是中国政府评估人命价值的标准吗？过去遇难男女的受扶养人是否曾得到过如此赔偿？在目前冲突中丧生人员的受扶养人是否得到了类似如此慷慨的补偿（如果有的话）？

如果工部局曾认真查找中国政府对人命价值的评估，它本可以从《字林西报》的专栏中发现，该报刊登了一则4月16日发自广州的报道，内容如下：
铁路灾难赔偿。
死者及伤者家属将获得现金。
广州，4月16日电
铁道部已向广东省政府通报了对去年1月广九铁路列车火灾受害者家属进行赔偿的措施，以供执行。
根据这些措施，每名遇难乘客的家属将获得100美元，每名受伤乘客将获得30美元。由于共有105名伤亡人员，赔偿总额为9,040美元。——《国民新闻》。
值得注意的是，家属的姓名和地址显然已经查明，并且是直接进行支付的。

旁观者
上海，10月13日

（右侧框内文字）
上海工部局
S. E. 登记处

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
OCT 1 2 1938

The Camp Riot :
Why Compensation ?

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—Come, render the account now
that the bill has been paid. What
pressure was brought to bear to
make the Municipal Council pay
$3,000 to the dependents of the men
killed at Kiaochow Road Camp? It
came out in evidence that the men
were out of hand for several months,
that the Council's employees were
acting in self-defence at the time
the men were killed, and that the
Chinese officers of the men in camp
were more or less responsible for the
trouble, because they could not control their men. Why then are these
men returned to the camp from
which they were taken, for the benefit of peace and order to the Settlement, which at the time of this uprising was costing the Council much
money to protect, and the residents
much inconvenience. Who demanded
the officers returned to the camp
and who pressed for the payment
for the dependents of the men killed?
This seems to me to be one of the
weakest settlements we have ever
been called upon to countenance, and,
since it is beyond the solving of even
the old-timers in China who thoroughly understand "face" and "loss
of face" it would be of interest
should your readers attempt to present the question glossed over by
the Council's attitude in a clearer
light!
Seems to me as though the spirits
of the men who were actually killed
in the godown from which this Lone
Battalion sprung into International
Settlement and ratepayers' heroes,
will stalk the Municipal Council's
Fathers, crying aloud for a $1,000
whisper into the ears of the supreme
Chinese General of war on their behalf, and that in future the three
heroes of the council of Kiaochow
Road will themselves advocate the
causes of the Chinese Ratepayers' Association in the realms above and
below, so grateful will they be for the
unsurpassed and unexpected foreign
man cumshaw.
DISGRACE.
Shanghai, Oct. 11.

《字林西报》，
1938年10月12日

营地骚乱：
为何赔偿？

致《字林西报》编辑

先生，——既然账单已付，现在就来算算账吧。究竟施加了什么压力，迫使工部局向胶州路营地遇难者的受扶养人支付3,000美元？证据显示，这些人几个月来一直难以管束，工部局雇员在他们被杀时是在自卫，而营地内这些人的中国军官对麻烦负有或多或少的责任，因为他们无法控制自己的部下。那么，为了租界的和平与秩序——当时工部局为此花费巨资进行保护，居民也深受不便之苦——为什么要把这些人送回他们原本被带出的营地？是谁要求将这些军官返回营地，又是谁为死者家属争取赔偿？在我看来，这是我们被迫容忍的最软弱的和解方案之一，既然这甚至超出了那些彻底理解“面子”和“丢脸”的中国老手所能解决的范畴，如果您的读者能尝试更清晰地揭示被工部局态度所掩盖的问题，那将是一件有趣的事！

在我看来，仿佛那些实际上在仓库中被杀之人的灵魂——正是从那里，这支孤军冲入国际租界并成为纳税人眼中的英雄——将在工部局董事们身边徘徊，大声哭喊，要求为他们向那位至高无上的中国战争将军耳边低语1,000美元，并且在未来，胶州路的三位英雄将在阴阳两界亲自倡导华人纳税会的事业，因为他们将对这笔无与伦比且出乎意料的外国人“赏赐”感激涕零。

DISGRACE
上海，10月11日

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,
OCT 8 1938

“Lone Battalion”
Trouble Settled

Compensation for Families
Of Men Killed in Riot at
Camp ; Officers Return

The Acting Secretary of the
Shanghai Municipal Council has
addressed the following letter to the
Chinese Ratepayers' Association. —

“I have to address you on the
subject of the unfortunate matter
that arose on August 11, at
Kiaochow Road Camp where certain
officers and men of the Chinese
Army were interned.

I am directed to state that the
Council most sincerely regrets that
circumstances were such that it was
forced to take the action it did. In
particular the Council sympathizes
deeply with the families of the three
men who unfortunately died of
injuries received in the affray.

On humanitarian grounds the
Council has decided to grant the sum
of $1,000 to the dependents of each
of the men who died of injuries.
Accordingly I have pleasure in en-
closing a cheque for $3,000, with
the request that your Association
ascertain the names and addresses
of the dependents properly entitled
to the money, and hand it over to
them.

Compassionate Grant

The Council is most anxious that
a state of affairs be brought about
by which harmonious relations will
subsist again between the Council's
officers responsible for guarding the
camp and the interned officers and
men. With this object in view the
Council has decided that the officers,
who at present are living apart from
the men, are to be allowed to return
to the Camp. It is the Council's
earnest hope that these officers will
assist the Council in carrying out the
extremely difficult and delicate task
imposed on the Council, through no
wish of its own, of keeping order
and discipline in the Camp.”

The officers were returned to the
Camp at 3.30 p.m. yesterday
from their temporary quarters on
in that employment has been found
The Bund.

《字林西报》，
1938年10月8日

“孤军”
风波平息

胶州路营地骚乱中
阵亡士兵家属获抚恤；
军官归队

上海公共租界工部局代理秘书致函华人纳税会，内容如下：——

“本人须就8月11日在胶州路营地发生的不幸事件致函贵会，当时该处拘禁着中国军队的部分官兵。

奉命声明，工部局对当时情势迫使该局采取上述行动深表遗憾。工部局特别对在冲突中不幸因伤身亡的三名士兵的家属致以深切慰问。

基于人道主义立场，工部局决定向每名因伤身亡士兵的受扶养人发放抚恤金1,000元。据此，本人谨随函附上支票一张，金额3,000元，并请贵会查明有权领取该款项的受扶养人的姓名及地址，并将款项转交予他们。

恩恤拨款

工部局极盼能促成一种局面，使负责守卫营地的工部局人员与被拘禁的官兵之间恢复和谐关系。为此目的，工部局决定允许目前与士兵分开居住的军官返回营地。工部局诚挚希望这些军官能协助工部局完成一项极其困难且微妙的任务，即维持营地内的秩序与纪律，此任务并非工部局所愿，却不得不承担。”

昨日下午3时30分，军官们已从外滩的临时住所返回营地。

CHINA PRESS.

SEP 25 1938

Repatriation Impossible
Talks Said Under Way But
Lone Battalion To Remain

Reports that the Shanghai Municipal Council was considering the repatriation of members of the "Lone Battalion" were categorically denied by Mr Eugene Y. B. Kiang, prominent local attorney and S.M.C. councillor, who is at present negotiating with Mr Cornell S Franklin, chairman of the S.M.C., on the future status of the interned soldiers.

Mr Kiang has already held several lengthy conversations with Mr Franklin regarding the soldiers since the S.M.C. chairman's return recently While he denied that there was even a remote possibility of the soldiers being returned to their native homes, as the Chinese press would have it, he voiced hope that the "Lone Battalion" problem may be settled quickly and to the complete satisfaction of all concerned.

"The best that can be done," Mr Kiang informed THE CHINA PRESS, "is to bring the Council and the soldiers together on a basis of mutual understanding."

The "Lone Battalion," it will be recalled, recently clashed with the Russian volunteers over a dispute concerning the hoisting of a Chinese National flag in their Kiaochow Road Camp in commemoration of the first anniversary of the outbreak of hostilities in Shanghai last August 12. In the subsequent fracas several of the interned soldiers were fatally wounded in the baton charges of the Russian Regiment.

To prevent similar disturbances, it will be remembered, the S.M.C. decided to separate the officers from their men.

1938年9月25日

遣返无望
称谈判正在进行，但
孤军仍将留驻

当地著名律师、工部局董事江一平（Eugene Y. B. Kiang）断然否认了有关上海公共租界工部局正考虑遣返“孤军”成员的报道。江一平目前正与工部局主席富兰克林（Cornell S Franklin）就被拘禁士兵的未来地位问题进行谈判。

自工部局主席近期返沪以来，江一平已就士兵问题与富兰克林先生进行了数次长谈。虽然江一平否认如中文报纸所称士兵有被送回原籍的任何可能性，但他表示希望“孤军”问题能迅速得到解决，令各方完全满意。

江一平告诉《大美晚报》：“目前所能做的最佳方案，是在相互理解的基础上，促使工部局与士兵达成一致。”

众所周知，“孤军”最近在胶州路营地因悬挂中国国旗以纪念去年8月12日上海战事爆发一周年而与俄国志愿队发生冲突。在随后的混战中，几名被拘禁士兵在俄国军团警棍驱散行动中受致命伤。

为防止类似骚乱，据悉工部局此前决定将军官与士兵分开安置。

GETTING HOMESICK

《上海泰晤士报》

1938年9月24日

“孤军”思乡心切

华人居民请求
准许士兵离城

据中文媒体报道，最近因在胶州路营地悬挂中国国旗以纪念上海战事爆发一周年而与俄国志愿队发生冲突、导致数人重伤的“孤军”成员，可能会被要求前往各自原籍长期休整。

上海的华人团体可能会向上海公共租界工部局请愿，请求批准为营员提供旅费，使他们能够回家，而不是留在最近发生骚乱的胶州路营地。

据称，工部局的华董已与外籍同僚讨论此事，请求允许士兵返乡，但未取得结果。

报道称，在最近一次工部局会议上并未讨论此问题，但在会后就此主题进行了非正式的意见交换。非正式会议在友好气氛中举行，但未达成明确解决方案。解决此事的细节可能在一周内确定。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

SEP 1 1938

The Lone Battalion
WITH THE RETURN to Shanghai of Mr.
C.S. Franklin, American chairman of the
Shanghai Municipal Council, it is expected that
a final settlement of the dispute between the
municipal authorities and the interned Chinese
"Lone Battalion" will be forthcoming.
A great deal of feeling was stirred up among
Chinese local residents over this case, which
had many unfortunate aspects. Some time has
now elapsed, and with the cooling of hot heads
and a chance for sane discussion by sympathetic
and neutral foreign municipal leaders, there
is every reason to think that the matter can
be smoothed over.
One important change should be made, in
that there ought to be better liaison between
the interned men and the municipal authorities.
It is clear enough that the clash resulted chiefly
through a lack of full understanding, and such
a situation should never develop again. The
entire foreign community has nothing but ad-
miration for the character of the "Lone Bat-
talion." At the same time the "Lone Battalion"
must understand something of the difficulties
with which the S.M.C. is confronted on many
fronts and these difficulties should not, and
need not, be multiplied.
The fact must be faced that despite Japa-
nese hopes for an early settlement of the
"China incident" favorable to themselves, no-
thing of the sort seems even remotely in pro-
spect; which means that the interned battalion
must remain as guest of the municipality for
a while to come. Local Chinese have displayed
understanding in quashing efforts to make
political capital out of the recent clash. It
now remains to settle the matter finally and
to set up safeguards against any further mis-
understanding or trouble which can benefit
nobody.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》

1938年9月1日

孤军

随着上海公共租界工部局美籍主席富兰克林（C.S. Franklin）返回上海，预计市政当局与被拘禁的中国“孤军”之间的纠纷即将得到最终解决。此案在华籍居民中激起了强烈情绪，其诸多方面令人遗憾。如今一段时间已过，随着头脑冷静下来，以及富有同情心且中立的外籍市政领袖有机会进行理性讨论，我们有充分理由相信此事可以得到缓和。

应当做出一个重要改变，即被拘禁人员与市政当局之间应建立更好的联络机制。显然，冲突主要是由于缺乏充分理解造成的，这种情况绝不应再次发生。整个外侨社群对“孤军”的品格唯有钦佩之情。同时，“孤军”必须理解工部局在多方面面临的困难，这些困难不应、也无需进一步加剧。

必须面对这样一个事实：尽管日本希望早日解决对其有利的“中国事变”，但此类前景似乎遥不可及；这意味着被拘禁的营队在接下来的一段时间内仍须作为市政当局的客人留驻。当地华人在遏制利用最近冲突谋取政治资本的努力方面表现出了理解。现在剩下的任务是最终解决此事，并设立保障措施，防止任何进一步的误解或麻烦，因为这对任何人都没有好处。

pages.en:
A DAILY NEWS.

8EP 7 13 'P

Settlement Looms
In Camp Dispute

Return of Mr. Franklin
Awaited ; Yu Ya Ching
Sees General Hsieh

A satisfactory solution of the dispute between the interned members of the Chinese so-called "Lone Battalion" and the Municipal authorities is awaited with the return of Mr. C. S. Franklin, Chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, from holiday on September 13. The way towards a settlement has been paved, it is understood, at a series of conferences between Mr Yu Ya-ching, a member of the Council, and General Hsieh Chin-yuan, the commander of the interned unit. These negotiations have now been completed.

A sanguinary riot of the "Lone Battalion" took place at their camp near Kiaochow Park on August 11, just preceding the first anniversary of the "Shanghai incident," and caused several deaths and the injury of scores of the Chinese soldiers and their Russian guards. The trouble, which had long been brewing, came to a head over the unauthorized hoisting, by the Chinese, of a large national flag. When members of the Russian Regiment, armed only with batons, were ordered by the camp commandant to remove the flag and flag-pole they were attacked with bottles, bamboos and other weapons obtained by the internees.

Hunger Strike Fails

After this battle the approximately 350 Chinese soldiers went on a hunger strike, which they however soon afterwards abandoned. For the sake of discipline the Chinese commander and his officers were removed from the camp and placed in rooms of the Russian Regiment barracks on The Bund. There has been no trouble at the camp since, although Chinese military internees in the French Concession rioted a few days after the Kiaochow Park revolt.

The "Lone" or "Doomed" Battalion, as will be recalled by many in Shanghai, was the Chapei unit which was caught in a large godown, in Chinese territory, at the corner of North Thibet Road and North Soochow Road, when other Chinese troops evacuated Chapei last October. They were hemmed in by the Japanese on three sides while on the fourth they faced the British military sector in West Hongkew. They were finally liberated through the British sector late at night, taken to the Race Course under guard and thence to the internment camp off Kiaochow Road.

Although the members of the unit were described as crack troops of the 88th Division of the Chinese National Army, many of them when seen at close range turned out to be gawky youths in their teens. Their commander, Colonel Hsieh, was promoted to "general" over-night.
pages.zh:
《每日新闻》

1938年9月7日

营地纠纷
有望解决

等待富兰克林归来；
虞洽卿会见谢将军

随着上海公共租界工部局主席富兰克林（C. S. Franklin）先生于9月13日度假归来，人们期待被拘禁的中国所谓“孤军”成员与市政当局之间的纠纷能得到圆满解决。据悉，通过工部局董事虞洽卿（Yu Ya-ching）与被拘禁部队指挥官谢晋元（Hsieh Chin-yuan）将军之间的一系列会议，和解之路已经铺平。这些谈判现已完成。

8月11日，就在“上海事变”一周年纪念日前夕，“孤军”在胶州公园附近的营地发生血腥骚乱，导致数名中国士兵及其俄国守卫死亡，数十人受伤。这场酝酿已久的冲突因中国人擅自悬挂大幅国旗而爆发。当仅配备警棍的俄国军团成员奉营地指挥官之命移除国旗和旗杆时，遭到了被拘禁者用瓶子、竹竿及其他武器发起的攻击。

绝食抗议失败

此次战斗后，约350名中国士兵开始绝食，但不久后便放弃。为了维持纪律，中国指挥官及其军官被移出营地，安置在外滩俄国军团兵营的房间内。此后营地未再发生骚乱，尽管在胶州公园暴动几天后，法租界内的中国军事被拘禁者发生了骚乱。

许多上海人还记得，这支“孤军”或称“敢死队”是闸北部队，去年10月其他中国军队撤离闸北时，他们被困在北西藏路与北苏州路转角处中国领土上的一座大仓库内。他们在三面被日军包围的情况下，第四面面向西虹口英军防区。最终，他们在深夜通过英军防区获得解放，在押送下前往跑马厅，随后被转移至胶州路外的拘禁营。

虽然该部队成员被描述为中国国民革命军第88师的精锐部队，但近距离观察发现，其中许多人竟是十几岁的笨拙青年。他们的指挥官谢团长一夜之间被晋升为“将军”。

of the 88th Division, to any au-
thority outside of the International
Settlement. THE CHINA PRESS
learned yesterday.

While taking a tolerant view of
the incident, British authorities
here yesterday pointed out that the
Chinese soldiers interned in the
Settlement were enjoying the
hospitality of the S.M.C. and the
protection of the S.M.C. They,
therefore, should have given more
consideration to the position of the
Council than to have taken action
which might have embarrassed not
only the Settlement, but the safety
of the "Lone Battalion" itself, it
was stated.

THE CHINA PRESS understands
that while the British Embassy
here has received no official protest
from the Chinese Government, it
has been approached in writing by
a number of organizations.

These communications are now
under consideration by the British
Ambassador, and will be replied to
in the near future.

日本发生了什么
致《字林西报》编辑

先生，——参照贵报今日第7版题为“对日本的侮辱态度”的文章，令我惊讶的是，《每日新闻》的作者如此无知，竟不知道在世界大战期间，特别是在1915年以及其他特殊场合（具体日期现已无法查证），在日本集中营中的德国战俘曾被允许在集中营内悬挂他们自己的国旗！尽管当时日本正与德国交战。《每日新闻》的那位煽动者应该问问自己，为什么工部局最近不允许“孤军”英雄们悬挂他们的旗帜。他们当然不能被剥夺国籍，也不能被剥夺对蒋介石政府的效忠；因此，他们完全有权使用他们的国旗。我与许多外国人交谈过，包括德国人，他们都不明白为什么工部局禁止展示国旗。这并非出于对任何国籍人士感情的尊重，除了日本人——仅仅是日本军方当局。《每日新闻》的作者显然在刻意损害日本人与本市其他国籍人士之间的友好关系。我不理解他的目的可能是什么。我可以这样说，没有人会反对对工部局行动的任何理智批评。给《每日新闻》作者的头脑降降温或许会有帮助。

V. P.
上海，8月17日。

Attitude Of
S. M. C. Over
Camp Affair

Official Answer To All
Protests Is Believed
Hardly Probable

COUNCIL TOOK ONLY
POSSIBLE STAND

Effort Will Be Put Forth
To Explain Situation To
Chinese Leaders

The official attitude of the Shanghai Municipal Council toward the protests which have been made by various Chinese public bodies in Shanghai regarding the "Lone Battalion" incident was explained here yesterday in a statement made by Mr. Stirling Fessenden, Secretary-General of the Council, to "The Shanghai Times."

Mr. Fessenden stated that it was unlikely that any formal answer would be given to the protests but an effort would be made to familiarize the officials of the various organizations which have made protests with the realities of the situation. It was further explained that discussions had already been held with a number of responsible Chinese.

In reviewing the events leading up to the incident, Mr. Fessenden stated that it would be necessary for those Chinese who had protested the intervention of the Russian Regiment to realize more fully the delicate situation which exists in Shanghai. The Shanghai Municipal Council, he indicated, has constantly attempted to minimize friction and maintain peace and order in the Settlement.

The official further explained that the request on the part of the "Lone Battalion" that it be allowed to fly a national flag was turned down on the grounds that it would only stir up trouble. The soldiers also wished to fly the flag so that it could easily be seen from the outside of the camp.

Were Not Invited

The Council did not wish to add to the tension prevailing at the time by allowing the soldiers to fly their flag, and, in any event, such a procedure with interned soldiers would have been almost unprecedented. In addition, the soldiers demanded that they be allowed to have firecrackers. Mr. Fessenden pointed out that these seemingly trivial incidents were but a climax to a long series of untoward circumstances in the camp.

He further explained that the Council would be only too glad to get rid of the "Lone Battalion" and that it had not invited the men into the settlement in the first place. With regard to reports that the present camp site might be changed, he stated that there was no apparent necessity for this and that the men would probably remain where they were.

In a local Chinese newspaper yesterday there appeared what purported to be an interview with Col. Hsieh Ching-yuan, former commanding officer of the "Lone Battalion," in which he reiterated his demands for the restoration of the flagpole, the punishment of the Russian Regiment and the payment of compensation to those Chinese who were injured.

工部局对
军营事件之态度

据信对所有抗议
作出正式答复
可能性极小

理事会仅采取
可行之立场

将努力向中国领袖
解释局势

上海公共租界工部局针对上海各中国公共团体就“孤军”事件所提出的抗议所持的官方态度，由工部局总办费信惇（Stirling Fessenden）先生昨日向《字林西报》（The Shanghai Times）发表声明予以说明。

费信惇先生表示，不太可能对这些抗议给予任何正式答复，但将努力使提出抗议的各组织官员了解局势的真实情况。此外还说明，已与若干负责任的中国人士进行了讨论。

在回顾导致该事件发生的经过时，费信惇先生指出，那些抗议俄国团介入的中国人士有必要更充分地认识到上海存在的微妙局势。他指出，上海公共租界工部局一直试图减少摩擦，维持租界内的和平与秩序。

该官员进一步解释说，“孤军”要求允许悬挂国旗的请求被驳回，理由是这只会引发麻烦。士兵们也希望悬挂国旗，以便从营区外部能够轻易看到。

未受邀请

工部局不愿因允许士兵悬挂旗帜而加剧当时普遍存在的紧张局势，而且无论如何，对被拘禁的士兵采取此类做法几乎是史无前例的。此外，士兵们还要求允许燃放鞭炮。费信惇先生指出，这些看似琐碎的事件不过是营区内长期发生的一系列不幸事件的高潮。

他进一步解释说，工部局非常乐意摆脱“孤军”，而且起初并未邀请这些人进入租界。关于目前营地可能搬迁的报道，他表示显然没有这种必要，这些人可能会留在原地。

昨日一家中文报纸刊登了一篇据称是对前“孤军”指挥官谢晋元上校的采访，他在采访中重申了其要求：恢复旗杆、惩处俄国团以及赔偿受伤的中国人的损失。

Don't Rock The Boat !
AN EDITORIAL in the Wuhan Jih Pao at
Hankow reminds us that the Chinese are
landlords and the Shanghai Municipal Council
only tenants. This as preliminary to some
bombastic remarks concerning the "Doomed
Battalion" here, with whose plight all neutrals
feel sympathy but with whose tactics most feel
impatience.
Very well. If the matter were to be dis-
missed so simply, the Council would have no
option other than to hand over the Interna-
tional Settlement to the Japanese who have
taken all surrounding territory and who lost
no time in seizing upon every available right
or privilege formerly granted the Chinese with-
in Council-controlled territory. Would that ap-
peal to any Chinese, in Shanghai or out of it?
The obvious fact is that the landlord-tenant
relation by no means represents the precise na-
ture of Nationalist China and the Settlement,
respectively, and such an organ as this Kuo-
mintang newspaper is hurting Chinese best
interests by such over-simplification which is
directly in line with the propaganda of the
Japanese. Somebody on the Wuhan Jih Pao
actually belongs on the Shanghai Nippo or
Mainichi.
Had the facts been as stated, Landlord
Nanking would have gobbled Tenant Shanghai
sometime between 1927 and 1937. Actually
Shanghai has contrived to remain a sort of
Switzerland, balanced precariously between the
devil and the deep blue sea for many a year,
and when the subject is viewed objectively over
a long period of time it must be seen by any
dispassionate person that this status has on
the whole worked out best for everybody
whether Chinese, Japanese, Briton, American
or any other nationality. Such being the case,
let's have a little less rocking of the boat.
