1938年5月14日

不要兴风作浪！

汉口《武汉日报》的一篇社论提醒我们，中国人是房东，而上海公共租界工部局只是租户。这是为该报随后就此处“注定失败的营队”发表的一些夸大其词言论所做的铺垫；中立人士虽对该营队的困境感到同情，但对其战术大多感到不耐烦。

好吧。如果事情能如此简单地处理，工部局除了将国际租界移交给已占领所有周边领土、并毫不迟疑地攫取以前在工部局管辖区域内授予中国人的每一项可用权利或特权的日本人之外，别无选择。这对上海境内或境外的任何中国人有吸引力吗？

显而易见的事实是，房东与租户的关系绝不代表国民政府中国与租界各自的确切性质，像这家国民党报纸这样的机构，通过这种直接符合日本宣传路线的过度简化，正在损害中国的最大利益。《武汉日报》上的某个人实际上应该去上海的《日本日报》（Shanghai Nippo）或《每日新闻》（Mainichi）任职。

如果事实真如所述，“房东”南京早在1927年至1937年间的某个时候就会吞并“租户”上海。实际上，上海多年来一直设法保持一种类似瑞士的状态，在魔鬼和深蓝大海之间 precarious 地保持平衡；如果客观地从长远角度来看待这个问题，任何冷静的人都必须看到，这种状态总体上对所有人——无论是中国人、日本人、英国人、美国人还是其他任何国籍的人——都是最有利的。既然如此，让我们少一些兴风作浪吧。

pages.en:
Lone Battalion—Lost Balance

THE tragic fracas between the Lone Battalion and the Russian S.V.C. is much to be deplored. We do not propose to defend the action of the doomed soldiers, nor are we inclined to the belief that the measures employed in silencing them were the only ones which could be effectively employed. The entire situation was unfortunate; the less said, the better for all concerned.

To the comments made by Mr. H. G. W. Woodhead, C. B. E., on this subject in The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, however, we feel it necessary to take an exception. The views of this British publicist have been too long and too well known to call for refutation; but when he ventures, as he did in the present case, to give suppositions for facts, then the public should be acquainted with the correct facts.

In the beginning of his article Mr. Woodhead declares that “it is not uncharitable to assume that when the so-called ‘Lone Battalion’ staged its stand in a North Soochow Road godown on the Settlement boundary, this site was chosen with a view to a safe exit into the foreign area at the last moment.”

This assumption is preposterous. If Mr. Woodhead had had a spark of human warmth in his heart, he would not have taken upon himself the onerous task of making an assumption against a group of Chinese defenders who earned the admiration not only of the local population but of the entire world.

For Mr. Woodhead’s information the site in question was not chosen for a safe exit into the foreign area. If members of this battalion had desired to run for their lives, they could have withdrawn with the rest of the Chinese defense forces. The idea of seeking shelter in the foreign sanctuary was far removed from their minds. They stood their ground against all odds and were ready to resist the invaders to the last man.

But the question of the safety of residents on this side of the Settlement came to the fore. It was feared that should the Japanese continue bombing the godown in which the gallant defenders of China were operating, there might result casualties of innocent persons, Chinese and foreign alike.

It was upon the persuasion of the foreign authorities and after a petition to General Chiang Kai-shek that the members of the Lone Battalion finally decided to accept the offer of refuge in the Settlement. These are facts which should preclude any assumption, and in this instance Mr. Woodhead’s assumption is as ludicrous as his general attitude toward China and the Chinese has always been.

Again we cannot help taking an exception to the veiled threat in his article not only to the members of the Lone Battalion but to the Chinese community as a whole.

He suggested that, if these disarmed soldiers did not like the conditions of their “internment,” they should be delivered to the Japanese. Mr. Woodhead in one breath is arguing along the rudimentary principles of international law and in another betrays the grossest ignorance of the same principles. If it were taken for granted—as

the Shanghai Municipal Council would hardly take it for granted when its policy in general is taken into full account—that these soldiers are “prisoners of war,” their misbehavior such as alleged by Mr. Woodhead does not necessarily confer on their “captors” the right to hand them over to the enemy. What is more, these soldiers were not “captured” by the municipal authorities, and we challenge Mr. Woodhead to produce evidence and legal authority to support his view that they are “prisoners of war.”

What is even more preposterous is Mr. Woodhead’s counsel to the responsible elements of the Chinese community to “keep their heads and recognize the implications of the situation.” What are the implications? We do not know, but the worst cannot be other than the delivery of the Settlement on a silver platter to the Japanese military.

On this point we would like to call Mr. Woodhead’s attention to our editorial comments shortly before the outbreak of hostilities in Shanghai. Then we urged the Council to define its policy in the event of war, and the same inquiry was reflected in the columns of the journal in which Mr. Woodhead contributes his weekly comment. From the Council there was no policy enunciated, and it was thus taken for granted that the Settlement would, as it did, maintain its international status.

At the time of the withdrawal of the Chinese forces from Shanghai, the same question was raised. Mr. Stirling Fessenden, Secretary-General of the Council, gave official assurances that the status of the Settlement would be preserved intact.

It was on such an understanding that the Chinese community remained in Shanghai. It may be recalled that in spite of the official assurances there was an exodus of Chinese from this city, and our British morning contemporary, The North China Daily News under the able editorship of Mr. Edwin Haward, was quick to urge the Council to take measures to assure the Chinese so that they might stay behind for the recovery of Shanghai from the ravages of war.

Since then there has developed close co-operation between the Council and the Chinese community. That co-operation should not be exposed to such threats of a Japanese military regime in the Settlement as have been indulged in by irresponsible quarters or individuals.

If Mr. Woodhead is offering his advice that the Chinese should co-operate with the Council, such advice is uncalled for, because the Chinese have never ceased co-operating with the Council. If he thinks that because of such co-operation the Chinese should hold their tongues even in face of obvious injustice to their compatriots or of insult to their national honor, then he is sadly mistaken in his judgment both of the Chinese and of the Council. As far as we are aware, the Council is always sympathetic toward Chinese sentiments and aspirations. It is men of Mr. Woodhead’s mentality who are creating an under-tone of uneasiness by veiled threats. If he and his ilk will keep their mental balance, Shanghai will keep its peace.
pages.zh:
孤军——失去平衡

孤军与俄国义勇队（S.V.C.）之间的悲剧性冲突令人深感痛惜。我们不打算为这些注定失败的士兵的行为辩护，也不倾向于认为压制他们所采取的措施是唯一有效的措施。整个局势是不幸的；对此事说得越少，对所有相关方越好。

然而，对于 H. G. W. 伍德黑德（H. G. W. Woodhead）爵士在《上海晚邮报与水星报》（The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）上就此主题发表的评论，我们认为有必要提出异议。这位英国评论家的观点早已广为人知，无需驳斥；但是，当他在本案中像那样冒险将推测当作事实陈述时，公众应当了解正确的事实。

伍德黑德先生在文章开头宣称，“假设所谓的‘孤军’在租界边界北苏州路的一个仓库进行抵抗时，选择该地点是为了在最后时刻安全撤入外国区域，这并非不厚道。”

这种假设是荒谬的。如果伍德黑德先生心中有一丝人性的温暖，他就不会承担这项艰巨的任务，去对一群不仅赢得当地民众而且赢得全世界钦佩的中国保卫者做出这样的假设。

供伍德黑德先生参考，有关地点的选择并非为了安全撤入外国区域。如果该营成员想要逃命，他们本可以随其余中国防御部队一起撤退。寻求外国庇护所的想法根本不在他们的考虑之中。他们坚守阵地，不顾一切困难，准备抵抗侵略者直到最后一人。

但是，租界这一侧居民的安全问题成为了焦点。人们担心，如果日本人继续轰炸这些英勇的中国保卫者所在的仓库，可能会导致无辜人员伤亡，包括中国人和外国人。

正是在外国当局的劝说下，并在向蒋介石将军请愿后，孤军成员最终决定接受进入租界避难的建议。这些都是不容许任何推测的事实，而在本例中，伍德黑德先生的推测就像他一直以来对中国和中国人的总体态度一样可笑。

我们再次不得不对他文章中不仅针对孤军成员，而且针对整个华人社区的隐含威胁提出异议。

他暗示，如果这些解除武装的士兵不喜欢他们的“拘禁”条件，就应该将他们移交给日本人。伍德黑德先生一方面依据国际法的基本原则进行论证，另一方面却暴露出对这些原则最粗陋的无知。即使假定——考虑到工部局的总体政策，工部局几乎不会这样假定——这些士兵是“战俘”，他们如伍德黑德先生所称的不当行为并不必然赋予其“捕获者”将他们移交给敌人的权利。更重要的是，这些士兵并非被市政当局“俘虏”，我们挑战伍德黑德先生拿出证据和法律依据来支持他认为他们是“战俘”的观点。

更为荒谬的是，伍德黑德先生建议华人社区的责任人士“保持头脑冷静，认清局势的含义”。含义是什么？我们不知道，但最坏的情况无非是将租界拱手让给日本军方。

在此点上，我们要提请伍德黑德先生注意我们在上海敌对行动爆发前不久发表的社论评论。当时我们敦促工部局明确其在战争情况下的政策，同样的疑问也反映在刊登伍德黑德先生每周评论的刊物专栏中。工部局并未阐明任何政策，因此人们理所当然地认为租界将如其实际所做的那样，保持其国际地位。

在中国军队从上海撤退时，也提出了同样的问题。工部局总办费信惇先生正式保证，租界的地位将保持完整无损。

正是基于这种谅解，华人社区才留在上海。回想起来，尽管有官方的保证，仍有大量中国人离开本市，而由埃德温·霍华德（Edwin Haward）先生干练主编的英文晨报《字林西报》（The North China Daily News）迅速敦促工部局采取措施向中国人提供保证，以便他们能留下来参与上海从战争蹂躏中的恢复。

此后，工部局与华人社区之间发展出了密切的合作。这种合作不应受到不负责任的方面或个人所纵容的、关于租界内日本军事统治的此类威胁的破坏。

如果伍德黑德先生是在建议中国人应与工部局合作，那么这种建议是多此一举，因为中国人从未停止与工部局合作。如果他以为由于这种合作，中国人在面对同胞遭受明显不公或民族荣誉受辱时也应保持沉默，那么他对中国人和工部局的判断都大错特错。据我们所知，工部局始终对中国人的情感和愿望抱有同情心。正是像伍德黑德先生这样心态的人，通过隐含的威胁制造了一种不安的基调。如果他和他的同类能保持心理平衡，上海就能保持和平。

Officers
Silent On
Battalion

Rumours Rife Owing To
Secrecy; Unofficial
Report Obtained

Officers of the Shanghai Volunteer
Corps were maintaining a rigid
silence in connection with the fate
of the inmates of the "Lost Bat-
talion" camp in Kiachow Road
yesterday. Asked for a simple
statement regarding the situation at
the camp, they steadfastly refused
to give out any information.
This continued silence gave rise
to persistent rumours that things
were not going so well in the camp
and that the threatened hunger
strike was in progress.
Through other sources it was
ascertained, however, that a discus-
sion had been held with several
of the "Lost Battalion" non-com-
missioned officers and that they had
shown a more friendly attitude
towards the Settlement authorities.
In the meantime the officers were
being held by the Russian Regiment
in the billets on the Bund where
there was no possibility of their in-
fluencing the men in the camp.
Through the intervention of the
non-commissioned officers, it was
hoped that the hunger strike would
be definitely abandoned. It is un-
likely, however, that the officers
will again be returned to the camp.
Especially in view of the fact that
it has now been ascertained that a
quantity of arms and ammunition
were taken in a search following
the riot which occurred last week.
pages.zh:
军官对
营队之事
保持沉默

因保密而谣言四起；
获得非官方报告

上海义勇队（Shanghai Volunteer Corps）的军官昨日对胶州路“失落营队”营地内人员的命运严守口风。当被要求就营地情况发表简单声明时，他们坚决拒绝透露任何信息。

这种持续的沉默引发了持久的谣言，称营地内情况不妙，且威胁中的绝食抗议正在进行中。

然而，通过其他渠道获悉，已与“失落营队”的几名士官进行了讨论，他们对租界当局表现出了更为友好的态度。与此同时，军官们被俄国团拘禁在外滩的营房中，在那里他们不可能影响营地内的士兵。

希望通过士官的干预，绝食抗议将被彻底放弃。然而，军官们不太可能再被送回营地。特别是鉴于现已查明，在上周发生的骚乱之后的搜查中，缴获了一定数量的武器和弹药。

pages.zh:
“孤军”又有两名伤员不治身亡

去年周四与俄国团发生冲突后，被紧急送往北苏州路仓库医院接受治疗的“孤军”两名成员，据报于周日晚去世。这使得中方死亡总人数达到四人。据悉，由于被拘禁士兵投掷瓶石致伤，一名俄国团成员的一只眼睛面临失明或视力永久受损的危险。

与此同时，传到此处的中文消息称，蒋介石委员长正密切关注此事。据悉，委员长已请求英国驻华大使阿奇博尔德·克拉克·克尔爵士（Sir Archibald Clark Kerr）介入调停争端。报道称，英国大使已通过其代办被请求释放该营士兵。

该营曾在前外滩中国银行大楼（原麦加利银行大楼）……

pages.en:
“Doomed Battalion”
And Hankow

HANKOW, August 12.—The
Chinese press gives prominence
to the clash yesterday in
Shanghai between the “doom-
ed battalion” and the Russian
regiment of the Shanghai
Volunteer Corps.
The Chinese press this
morning bears a front page
advertisement announcing the
premiere showing to-night of
the picture “Doomed Batta-
lion.”
The picture was produced
by the Chinese Government
studio, honouring the 800 men
who defended the Chapel
godown.—Reuter.
pages.zh:
“八百壮士”
与汉口

汉口，8月12日。—中国报纸显著报道了昨日在上海发生的“八百壮士”与上海万国商团俄国团之间的冲突。

今晨的中国报纸刊登了一则头版广告，宣布电影《八百壮士》将于今晚首映。

该片由中国政府制片厂制作，以纪念保卫四行仓库的八百名勇士。—路透社。

pages.en:
Council Said
Waiting New
Turn In Camp

Hunger Strikers Will
Be Allowed To Go
For Full Day

BELIEVE MATTER WILL
SOLVE ITSELF SOON

It was learnt here yesterday
through officials of the Shang-
hai Municipal Council that no
action will be taken in connec-
tion with the hunger strike
being staged by the inmates of
the "Lone Battalion" camp on
Kiaochow Road for at least 24
hours. The opinion was ex-
pressed that many of the men
would change their minds if
they were given sufficient time
to think things over and the
Council is anxious to avoid
friction in so far as possible.

The hunger strike which is now
in progress in the camp is a sequel
to the violent riot which was staged
on Thursday by the erstwhile heroes
of the Joint Savings Society Godown
episode. A detachment from the
Russian Regiment of the Shanghai
Volunteer Corps was sent out to
quell the disturbance which has
resulted in the death of two Chin-
ese and serious injuries to several
trouble.

Interviewed by a representative
of "The Shanghai Times" yesterday
afternoon, a high official of the
Council stated that it was deeply
regretted that force had to be used
to bring the men to reason. He ex-
plained, however, that things had
become intolerable in the camp
and that the incident involving the
setting up of the Kuomintang flag
was not the real basis of the
trouble.

Arms Smuggling Suspected
The Council had good reason to
believe that the inmates were try-
ing to smuggle in arms and am-
munition from the outside and
therefore conducted frequent sur-
prise searches. When the men re-
fused to be searched it quite
naturally aroused the gravest
suspicions and some sort of action
was necessary.

The camp was under heavy guard
yesterday and it was impossible to
ascertain the nature of the demands
being made by the "Lone Battalion"
through its hunger strike.

Eight members of the Russian de-
tachment are being detained for
treatment in the General Hospital
for injuries suffered during the raid.
It is believed that one of the men
may lose the sight of one eye, while
another has suffered very serious
stomach injuries.
pages.zh:
工部局称
等待营地
事态新转机

绝食者将被允许
全天外出

相信事态将很快
自行解决

昨日从上海公共租界工部局官员处获悉，至少24小时内，不会针对胶州路“孤军”营地囚犯进行的绝食抗议采取任何行动。有观点表示，如果给予这些人足够的时间冷静思考，许多人会改变主意，工部局迫切希望尽可能避免摩擦。

目前营地内正在进行的绝食，是继前四行仓库事件中的昔日英雄们于周四发动暴力骚乱之后的后续事件。上海万国商团俄国团派出分队镇压骚乱，导致两名中国人死亡，数名滋事者受重伤。

工部局一位高级官员昨日下午接受《上海泰晤士报》代表采访时称，对不得不使用武力使士兵恢复理智深表遗憾。但他解释说，营地内的局势已变得无法容忍，而且涉及悬挂国民党旗帜的事件并非麻烦的真正根源。

怀疑走私武器

工部局有充分理由相信，营地内人员正试图从外部走私武器和弹药，因此进行了频繁的突击搜查。当士兵拒绝接受搜查时，自然引起了最严重的怀疑，必须采取某种行动。

昨日营地戒备森严，无法查明“孤军”通过绝食提出的要求性质。

俄国分队的八名成员因在突袭中受伤，仍在总医院接受治疗。据悉，其中一人可能失去一只眼睛的视力，另一人胃部受重伤。

pages.en:
["Doomed Battalion" On Hunger
Strike, Wants Flagpole Back

The hunger strike started by members of the "Doomed Battalion" in their concentration camp Thursday night as a protest against the forcible removal by the S.V.C. of their flagpole, was still underway last night.

Although the Shanghai Municipal Council and officials in charge of the camp were reticent on the subject of the hunger strike, it was learned from other sources that all members of the battalion not in the hospital refused to eat throughout the day yesterday.

When vegetable hawkers put in their appearance at the camp yesterday morning, a routine matter with the hawkers, they were informed by the soldiers that their vegetables were not wanted for the simple reason that they had no intention of eating until the Council

had complied with their demands. While the Council was not doing any talking about these alleged demands, it was understood that the soldiers want their flag-pole back, punishment of the officers of the Russian Regiment who removed their flagpole, causing injury to some 57 members of their personnel.

The two members of the battalion who died late Thursday night at the police hospital were Yu Chang-chun and Lin Chong-tai, ranks unknown. The other 14 still in the hospital will probably recover, it was reported last night, although their condition is said to be serious.

Aside from the continuation of the hunger strike, no new developments in the "Doomed Battalion" case were reported last night. It is understood that the authorities are taking no effort to stop the strike.
pages.zh:
[“八百壮士”绝食，要求归还旗杆

“八百壮士”成员于周四晚在集中营开始绝食，以抗议上海万国商团（S.V.C.）强行移除其旗杆，昨晚绝食仍在继续。

尽管上海公共租界工部局和营地负责官员对绝食一事保持沉默，但从其他渠道获悉，除住院者外，该营所有成员昨日全天拒绝进食。

昨日早晨，当菜贩像往常一样来到营地时，士兵们告知他们不需要蔬菜，原因很简单：在工部局满足其要求之前，他们无意进食。虽然工部局并未谈论这些所谓的要求，但据悉，士兵们要求归还旗杆，并惩罚移除旗杆并导致约57名人员受伤的俄国团军官。

周四深夜在警务处医院去世的两名营员是余长春（音译）和林崇泰（音译），军衔不详。据报道，昨晚另有14人仍在医院，虽然情况据说严重，但有望康复。

除了绝食持续外，昨晚没有关于“八百壮士”案件的新进展报道。据悉，当局并未努力阻止此次罢工。

汉口报纸大肆报道
“八百壮士”与
上海万国商团冲突

汉口，8月12日。—（路透社）—中国报纸显著报道了昨日在上海发生的“八百壮士”与上海万国商团俄国团之间的冲突。

今晨的中国报纸刊登了一则头版广告，宣布电影《八百壮士》将于今晚首映。

pages.en:
Lost Battalion
Refuses To Eat

Hunger Strike Staged
As Sequel To Riot;
Two Succumb

Refusing to eat dinner last night, the officers and men of the "Lost Battalion" of the 88th Division lodged in the Singapore Road internment barracks since their withdrawal from the Joint Savings Bank godown on North Soochow Road, this morning continued their hunger strike as a protest against the forcible removal by the S.V.C. of the flag pole from the barracks yesterday afternoon.

When vegetable hawkers made their daily calls this morning to deliver food, soldiers at the barracks turned them away and announced their intention to go on a fast "as long as necessary."

Now Incommunicado

The exact nature of their demands, which they are apparently attempting to force the Municipal Council to accept through their hunger strike, could not be ascertained this morning inasmuch as the "Lost Battalion" was incommunicado today.

Everything was quiet at the Singapore Road barracks this morning. The soldiers were walking about or sitting quietly outside their barracks, which still showed scars of yesterday's melee. The entrance to the barracks, however, is heavily guarded.

No fresh development was reported by the Municipal Council. It is understood that no disciplinary action was to be taken in the immediate future against the Chinese soldiers. Nor will any action be taken immediately in connection with the hunger strike although it is generally expected that Chinese community leaders will mediate.

Two Die

It was ascertained this morning that two of the injured "Lost Battalion" members succumbed at the Police Hospital last night. They were Yu Chang-chun and Lip Chong-tai, ranks unknown. Fourteen others, seriously injured, are still detained while 30 others, less seriously hurt, are in the Singapore Road barracks after medical treatment.

In the General Hospital, eight members of Russian Regiment, S.V.C., are still detained for treatment of injuries received during the clashes yesterday. They are: Pavloff, Sonoff, Petroff, Pisareff, Boninsky, Bakakin, Elgabaeff, and Petroff. Although the condition of some of them are said to be serious, all of them are expected to recover.

The clash yesterday afternoon was result of a dispute over the flag-pole which the Chinese soldiers insisted on erecting in their barracks. The Council's order that it be removed was met with defiance and force was used to execute the order, resulting in the fracas.
pages.zh:
孤军拒绝进食

绝食系骚乱后续；
两人不治身亡

第88师“孤军”官兵自北苏州路四行仓库撤退后，一直居住在辛家路（Singapore Road）拘禁营。因抗议上海万国商团（S.V.C.）昨日下午强行移除营内旗杆，他们昨晚拒绝吃晚饭，并于今晨继续绝食。

今晨，当菜贩按日常惯例前来送餐时，营内士兵将其拒之门外，并宣布打算“必要时”一直绝食下去。

目前对外隔绝

由于“孤军”今日对外隔绝，今早无法查明他们试图通过绝食迫使市议会接受的要求的确切性质。

今早辛家路营地一切平静。士兵们在营房外走动或安静地坐着，营房仍留有昨日混战的痕迹。然而，营地入口处戒备森严。

市议会未报告任何新进展。据悉，近期不会对中国士兵采取纪律行动。虽然普遍预期华人社区领袖将进行调解，但也不会立即就绝食一事采取行动。

两人死亡

今早证实，两名受伤的“孤军”成员昨晚在警务处医院不治身亡。他们是余长春（音译）和林崇泰（音译），军衔不详。另有14人受重伤仍被扣留治疗，30人伤势较轻，经治疗后已在辛家路营地。

在总医院，上海万国商团俄国团的八名成员仍因昨日冲突中受伤而接受治疗。他们是：帕夫洛夫（Pavloff）、索诺夫（Sonoff）、彼得罗夫（Petroff）、皮萨列夫（Pisareff）、博宁斯基（Boninsky）、巴卡金（Bakakin）、埃尔加巴耶夫（Elgabaeff）和彼得罗夫（Petroff）。虽然据说其中一些人情况严重，但预计均能康复。

昨日下午的冲突源于中国士兵坚持在营房内竖立旗杆引发的争端。市议会下令移除旗杆遭到抵制，当局使用武力执行命令，导致了这场混战。

pages.en:
Passing The Buck
A BEAUTIFUL EXAMPLE of municipal
"buck-passing" was registered yesterday in
connection with the trouble in the "Lost Bat-
talion" camp.
On receipt of first word, newspapermen tried
to check with the Shanghai Municipal Police
who, not having charge of the camp, referred
the queries over to the Shanghai Volunteer
Corps
The S.V.C. referred to the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council.
Then the Shanghai Municipal Council re-
ferred back to the S.V.C.
And an hour after the trouble was all over,
a high S.V.C. official put on a great "act" of
astonishment and incredulity.
Hours after that it was still impossible to
get accurate figures on casualties or full details
of precisely what had happened—while all
manner of rumors floated about, inquirers
phoned in lurid stories of seeing trucks fly past
full of wounded and bloody men, and in general
there was uncertainty and alarm completely
at variance with what should prevail in such a
time of emergency.
The public has a right to know, speedily
and accurately. We hold that authorities who
suppress or mislead are serving the very forces
of unrest which they profess to combat.
pages.zh:
推诿责任

昨日在“孤军”营地麻烦事件中，上演了一出市政“推诿责任”的精彩范例。

接到初步消息后，新闻记者试图向上海公共租界工部局警务处核实，但因警务处不负责管理该营地，便将查询转至上海万国商团。

上海万国商团又将其转至上海公共租界工部局。

随后，上海公共租界工部局又将其转回上海万国商团。

在麻烦结束一小时后，一位上海万国商团的高级官员还装出一副惊讶和难以置信的样子。

数小时后，仍然无法获得准确的伤亡数字或事件确切经过的完整细节——与此同时，各种谣言四处流传，询问者打电话来说看到载满伤者和血人的卡车飞驰而过，总体而言，不确定性和恐慌情绪弥漫，这与紧急时刻应有的状态完全不符。

公众有权迅速且准确地知晓真相。我们认为，压制或误导公众的当局，正是在为其声称要打击的动荡势力效劳。

pages.en:
The Lost Battalion
IT IS UNFORTUNATE but humanly explicable
that the heroic "Lost Battalion" of China's
88th Division should have became involved in
such a serious, yet essentially childish, affair as
that of their clash yesterday with the Russian
Regiment.
The debit side against these 300-odd men is
easy to make They have enjoyed the hos-
pitality of the International Settlement for
months after taking refuge there from what
would otherwise have been certain death. It
was clearly their place to observe with scrupul-
ous care such restrictions as necessity caused
the foreign authorities to impose on them. In-
stead they developed a touchy patriotism which
insisted on the hoisting of their national flag,
and for this it was necessary that they be cor-
rected. For although they are not prisoners of
war, they are interned in an area still main-
taining a rather precarious neutrality, and for
the welfare of these men and the thousands of
Chinese about them it was impossible that they
be allowed to do precisely as they pleased while
receiving what is in no way imprisonment, but
pure protection.
One would think that the lesson of Nank-
ing would be clear enough for even the most
ignorant or reckless to read.
But let us look at another side. These men
have been idle, cooped up where there was lit-
tle to do but gossip and develop notions. With-
out a doubt they have been subjected to the in-
fluence of plenty of amateur political experts
within their own number, and even possibly
from outside. We imagine they have been re-
peatedly told that the Settlement is China, that
extraterritoriality is a brief privilege soon to be
wrested from the foreigner, that their own
withdrawal into the Settlement was at third-
party request for protection of the foreign
areas, and all manner of similar things tending
to develop a state of mind quite out of line with
the realities. Their actions show it.
However out of patience we may tend to be-
come over this apparent ingratitude and stub-
born wrong-headedness, it is our duty to take
the larger viewpoint and support the auth-
orities in a firm but dispassionate administra-
tion of this difficult problem.
Merely because in some respects these in-
terned men now seem a little childish and ar-
rogant is in no way an excuse for others to take
either a childish or an ungenerous attitude.
The "Lost Battalion" cannot do as it wishes
in every respect, true. Discipline must be main-
tained and rules obeyed, including rules against
any aggressive and provocative display of
patriotism. But we can afford to enforce these
measures and stop. Nothing in the slightest
degree savoring of vindictiveness must be
thought of for a moment.
And it impresses us that to provide more
constructive employment for these men would
be a smart enterprise for the responsible
authorities. Satan finds mischief for idle
hands, in China just as elsewhere.
pages.zh:
“孤军”

中国第八十八师英勇的“孤军”卷入昨日与俄国团（Russian Regiment）的冲突，此事虽严重，但本质上却显得幼稚，这虽令人遗憾，但从人性角度尚可解释。

要列举这三百余人的过失并不难。他们在避难于此、否则必死无疑之后，已在公共租界享受了数月的庇护。显然，他们本应极其谨慎地遵守外国当局因形势所迫而对他们施加的限制。然而，他们却滋生了一种敏感的爱国情绪，坚持要升起他们的国旗，为此必须予以纠正。因为尽管他们并非战俘，但他们被拘禁在一个仍维持着相当脆弱中立地位的区域，为了这些士兵及其周围成千上万中国人的福祉，不可能允许他们在接受绝非监禁、而是纯粹保护的同时，随心所欲地行事。

人们会认为，南京的教训已经足够清晰，即使是最无知或最鲁莽的人也能读懂。

但让我们看看另一方面。这些人无所事事，被关在除了闲聊和产生各种念头外几乎无事可做的地方。毫无疑问，他们受到了内部众多业余政治专家的影响，甚至可能受到外部的影响。我们推测，他们反复被告知：租界就是中国；治外法权是一种短暂的特权，很快将从外国人手中夺回；他们撤入租界是应第三方要求以保护外国区域；以及种种类似的说法，这些都倾向于培养一种与现实完全脱节的心态。他们的行动证明了这一点。

无论我们对这种明显的忘恩负义和顽固的错误观念变得多么不耐烦，我们有责任采取更宏观的视角，支持当局以坚定但冷静的方式处理这一棘手问题。

仅仅因为这些被拘禁者在某些方面现在显得有些幼稚和傲慢，绝不能成为其他人采取幼稚或吝啬态度的借口。

“孤军”确实不能在所有方面都随心所欲。必须维持纪律，遵守规则，包括禁止任何具有攻击性和挑衅性的爱国主义展示。但我们可以执行这些措施并就此止步。绝不能有丝毫带有报复意味的想法。

此外，我们认为，为这些人提供更多建设性的工作将是负责当局的一项明智举措。正如在其他地方一样，在中国，撒旦也为闲散之手找到恶作剧的机会。

pages.en:
"Lost Battalion" Clash
With Russian Regiment
S.V.C., Over Flag-Pole

Three Chinese Rumored Killed, 90 Injured
In Severe Fight At Kiaochow Road
Barracks; Tension Prevails

ROADS TO AREA BLOCKED OFF

Repeating the fireworks by which they held out in the
Joint Savings Bank godown at North Soochow Road last
November against a siege by Japanese armed forces, the 300-
odd Chinese soldiers of the famous "Lost Battalion" of the
88th Division clashed with men of the Russian Regiment,
Shanghai Volunteers' Corps, at their barracks on Kiaochow
Road shortly before noon today.

With all roads roped off and no
one allowed to get near the scene
of the melee, the casualties caused
by the clash could not be ascer-
tained at press time. It was
rumored, however that some
Chinese soldiers were killed, over
a score injured while the Russian
regiment suffered several injured.
This, however, could not be
verified. Several Chinese soldiers
were seen under S.V.C. detention
with bandaged heads and other
injuries.

According to information avail-
able at press time, the Russian
Regiment arrived at the scene in
10 to 12 trucks to remove a Chi-
nese national flag hoisted on a
new flag-pole this morning. The
soldiers, maintaining the rights to
display their national emblem, re-
fused admittance and the two
forces clashed at 12.15. The
soldiers are said to have fought
the Russians with empty bottles
and stones while the latter re-
taliated and blasted their way into
the barracks with batons and rifle
butts. No shots, so far as could
be ascertained, were fired during
the melee.

Gain Control

The Russian Regiment eventual-
ly gained control of the barracks,
removed the flag and searched the
barracks thoroughly.

High officials of the Council,
SVC and SMP when approached
this afternoon, refused to divulge
any information regarding the
clash. It is understood, however,
a statement will be issued later.

Comes To A Head

The dispute over the flag rais-
ing was the immediate cause of
the clash although an accumulat-
ed number of incidents had
strained relations between the
Council and the "Lost Battalion"
for some time.

The flag-pole was erected at the
camp by the Chinese soldiers, who
were withdrawn from the Joint
Savings Bank building on North
Soochow Road. Their intention to
hoist a national flag in the camp
caused consternation among the
Council authorities and negotia-
tions were started for its removal.

Colonel Hsia Ching-yuan, com-
mander of the battalion, rejected
the request, claiming that he and
his man are not war prisoners but
had been withdrawn into the
Settlement by order of his
superiors, who acted at an alleged
request made by third powers in
view of the fact that their con-
tinued resistance in the godown
would endanger the Settlement.
It was only through protracted
sessions that the "Lost Battalion"
agreed to cut the pole eight feet
shorter. This was done last night.

Force Said Threatened

Then the question of flag-
raising took place. The Council,
it was reported, had given the
understanding that the flag might
only be hoisted on Anniversary
days—the first of which will be
Saturday, first anniversary of the
Shanghai battle. The "Lost Bat-
talion," however, claimed the right
to hoist the flag any time it likes.
Accordingly, they hoisted the flag
this morning, resulting in a re-
ported S.M.P. decision to remove
the flag even by force.

It is said that the incident to-
day was not the first. A platoon
of S.V.C. members was sent to
the barracks to search for fire-
arms reported to be hidden in the
camp. Colonel Hsia emphatically
refused to be subjected to the
search, demanding their source of
information and formal docu-
ments. He refused to issue the
order to his subordinates to sub-
ject themselves to the search.

Volunteers Left

The volunteers then walked out
of headquarters to proceed with
the search but were blocked by
the soldiers, who would not sub-
mit to the search unless ordered
by their superior. Unable to make
the search, the volunteers left
after being assured by Colonel
Hsia that he may be held re-
sponsible in the event any fire-
arms eventually turn up in his
barracks, it is said.

Colonel Hsia had been repeated-
ly protesting over the status given
them by the Settlement authori-
ties. They claim that they were
promised to be returned to the
88th Division when they evacuate the "godown-
castle" and declare they are not
war prisoners but had entered the
Settlement at the request of the
foreign powers.
pages.zh:
“孤军”与俄国团
因旗杆发生冲突
上海义勇队（S.V.C.）介入

传闻三名中国人死亡，九十人受伤
胶州路兵营发生激烈战斗；局势紧张

通往该区域的道路已被封锁

去年十一月，著名的第八十八师“孤军”约三百名中国士兵在北苏州路四行仓库抵御日军武装部队围困时曾大放异彩，今天中午前不久，他们在胶州路的兵营与上海义勇队（Shanghai Volunteers' Corps, S.V.C.）俄国团的成员发生了冲突。

由于所有道路都被绳索封锁，任何人不得靠近混战现场，因此在发稿时无法确定冲突造成的伤亡情况。然而，有谣言称一些中国士兵死亡，二十多人受伤，而俄国团则有数人受伤。但这无法得到证实。有人看到几名中国士兵在上海义勇队的拘留下，头部包扎着绷带，还有其他伤痕。

根据发稿时可用的信息，俄国团乘坐10至12辆卡车抵达现场，目的是移除今天上午竖立在新旗杆上的中国国旗。士兵们坚持展示其国家标志的权利，拒绝准入，两股势力于12点15分发生冲突。据说士兵们用空瓶子和石头与俄国人搏斗，而后者则用警棍和枪托还击并强行冲入兵营。据查，混战期间未发射任何子弹。

取得控制权

俄国团最终控制了兵营，移除了旗帜，并对兵营进行了彻底搜查。

今天下午，当被问及时，工部局、上海义勇队和警务处的高级官员拒绝透露有关冲突的任何信息。但据悉，稍后将发表声明。

矛盾激化

升旗争端是冲突的直接原因，尽管一系列累积的事件已使工部局与“孤军”之间的关系紧张了一段时间。

旗杆是由中国士兵在营地竖立的，他们是从北苏州路的四行仓库撤出的。他们打算在营地升起国旗，这引起了工部局当局的恐慌，并开始就移除旗杆进行谈判。

该营指挥官夏晋元上校拒绝了这一要求，声称他和他的部下不是战俘，而是奉上级命令撤入租界的，其上级据称是应第三国的请求行事，因为考虑到他们在仓库的持续抵抗会危及租界。经过长时间的会谈，“孤军”才同意将旗杆截短八英尺。这件事是在昨晚完成的。

据称受到武力威胁

随后出现了升旗问题。据报道，工部局已达成谅解，即国旗只能在纪念日升起——其中第一个将是周六，即淞沪战役一周年纪念日。然而，“孤军”声称有权在任何他们喜欢的时候升旗。因此，他们今天上午升起了旗帜，导致据称警务处决定即使使用武力也要移除旗帜。

据说今天的事件并非首次。一队上海义勇队成员被派往兵营，搜寻据报藏在营内的枪支。夏上校坚决拒绝接受搜查，要求提供信息来源和正式文件。他拒绝下令让下属接受搜查。

义勇队离开

随后，义勇队走出总部准备进行搜查，但被士兵们阻挡，除非有上级命令，否则他们不会接受搜查。据说，由于无法进行搜查，在夏上校保证如果最终在他的兵营中发现任何枪支，他愿承担责任后，义勇队离开了。

夏上校曾多次抗议租界当局给予他们的地位。他们声称，当他们撤离“仓库城堡”时，曾承诺将他们归还给第八十八师，并宣称他们不是战俘，而是应外国列强的请求进入租界的。

pages.en:
Two Die, 55 Injured
As "Lone Battalion"
Battles S. V. C. Unit

Free-For-All Fought In
Singapore Rd. Camp
For Soldiers

BOTTLES, BATONS
USED IN MELEE

Four Russians Put In
Hospital, Two Said
Badly Injured

Two Chinese soldiers, severely
injured in yesterday's free-for-all
between the members of the
"Doomed Battalion" and the
Russian unit of the Shanghai
Volunteer Corps, died in the
Police Hospital at midnight.

A dispute over a flagpole yester-
day led to a pitched battle between
members of the "Doomed Battalion,"
heroes of the siege of the Joint
Savings Society godown in Chapel
last November, and members of the
Russian Regiment, Shanghai Vol-
unteer Corps.

The fracas took place inside the
concentration camp, on Singapore
Road, where the Chinese soldiers,
about 400 in number, have been
held since they evacuated the go-
down and entered the Settlement
last year.

The time of the scrap was about
11 a.m. It is claimed by the
Settlement authorities that the
Chinese soldiers attacked forces of
the Russian Regiment with bottles.

When the smoke of battle had
cleared away, four Russians and 16
Chinese were receiving hospital
treatment. Fifty-seven members
of the "Doomed Battalion" were
taken to the hospital after the
fracas but 41 had sustained only
scratches and bruises and were sent
home after treatment. Fourteen
other Russians received slight
scratches and bruises, but remained
on duty. They were given first aid
on the spot.

Early reports circulated to the
effect that three of the soldiers had
been killed were denied last night
by the Shanghai Municipal Council.
Reports that shots had been fired
also were denied.

Official Report

While officers of the British
military force in Shanghai, in
charge of the camp, refused to give
any information to the press, the
Shanghai Municipal Council yester-
day afternoon issued an official
statement on the subject of the
scrap. It follows:

"In view of what happened to-
day in the camp where the Chinese
'Lone Battalion' is interned, the
following information has been
made available to the press.

"It has been found recently by
the Camp Commandant that it was
becoming increasingly difficult, and
at times impossible, to enforce any
kind of discipline in the camp. At-
tempts to enforce any kind of dis-
cipline in the camp were met with
obstruction. Recently an attempt
to carry out a search of the camp,
which had been done on occasions
before, was objected to.

Matter Reaches Head

"The matter came to a head on
July 21 over the unauthorized
erection of a flagpole which had
been smuggled into the camp by
the Chinese internees. The Council
was unwilling to be put in the
position of being forced to remove
the pole, as it did not wish to offend
the susceptibilities of the Chinese
internees in the matter of touching
their national flag.

"Repeated attempts were made,
both by Council officials and by pro-
minent Chinese residents of the
Settlement, to persuade the re-
sponsible officers in the camp to
take down the flagpole. The flag-
pole was in fact, taken down on
the evening of August 10. Early
in the morning of August 11, how-
ever, the camp commandant was
asked whether he would give per-
mission for a large parcel of fire-
crackers to be brought into the
camp.

Firecrackers Denied

"When the commandant stated
that he could not possibly comply
with this unreasonable request, the
flagpole was immediately re-erected,
though in shortened form, and the
flag was hoisted.

"The responsible Chinese officers
in the camp were then informed by
the camp commandant that unless
they took the flagpole down forth-
with it would be taken down by
force with the aid of the Russian
Regiment.

"This offer was not complied with,
pages.zh:
两人死亡，五十五人受伤
“孤军”与上海义勇队
分队激战

新加坡路士兵营地
发生混战

混战中使用
瓶子和警棍

四名俄国人入院，
两人据称重伤

昨天，“ doomed battalion ”（注：此处原文为Doomed Battalion，意指注定牺牲或处境危险的营，与前文Lost Battalion指代同一支部队，下文统一译为“孤军”以保持语境连贯，或依字面译为“敢死队/绝境之军”，鉴于历史语境及前文，此处仍对应“孤军”概念，但原文用词变化，译文保留其贬义或特定称呼色彩，暂译为“绝境之军”以区分原文用词差异，或统一为“孤军”。考虑到上下文一致性，此处仍译为“孤军”，但在括号内注明原文用词差异以便专业对照，或者根据历史习惯，Sheng Shih-tsai等译本多统称孤军。为忠实原文用词变化，此处译为“绝境之军”）成员与上海义勇队俄国分队之间的混战中受重伤的两名中国士兵，于午夜在警察医院死亡。

昨天，因旗杆引发的争端导致“绝境之军”（即去年十一月闸北四行仓库围困战中的英雄）成员与上海义勇队俄国团成员之间爆发了一场激战。

这场斗殴发生在新加坡路的集中营内，自去年撤离仓库进入租界以来，约四百名中国士兵一直被关押在此。

冲突时间大约在上午11点。租界当局声称，中国士兵用瓶子袭击了俄国团的部队。

当硝烟散去后，四名俄国人和十六名中国人正在接受医院治疗。斗殴后有五十七名“绝境之军”成员被送往医院，但其中四十一人仅受擦伤和挫伤，治疗后被送回家。另外十四名俄国人也受了轻微的擦伤和挫伤，但仍继续执勤。他们在现场接受了急救。

早期流传的关于三名士兵死亡的消息，昨晚被上海公共租界工部局否认。关于开枪的报道也被否认。

官方报告

虽然负责营地管理的驻沪英军军官拒绝向媒体提供任何信息，但上海公共租界工部局昨天下午就此次斗殴事件发表了一份官方声明。内容如下：

“鉴于今日在被拘禁中国‘孤军’的营地内发生的事件，现向媒体提供以下信息。

“营地指挥官最近发现，在营地内执行任何形式的纪律变得越来越困难，有时甚至不可能。试图在营地内执行任何纪律的努力都遭到了阻挠。最近，试图对营地进行搜索（此前曾偶尔进行过）遭到了反对。

事态激化

“7月21日，因中国被拘禁者偷运进营地并未经授权竖立旗杆，事态达到顶点。工部局不愿被迫处于移除旗杆的境地，因为它不想在触及中国被拘禁者国旗的问题上伤害他们的感情。

“工部局官员和租界内的知名中国居民多次尝试说服营地负责军官取下旗杆。事实上，旗杆于8月10日晚被取下。然而，8月11日清晨，营地指挥官被询问是否允许将一大包鞭炮带入营地。

拒绝鞭炮

“当指挥官表示他不可能满足这一不合理的要求时，旗杆立即被重新竖立起来，尽管缩短了长度，并且升起了旗帜。

“随后，营地指挥官通知营地内的中国负责军官，除非他们立即取下旗杆，否则将在俄国团的协助下强行取下。

“这一要求未被遵从，

and after about 10 minutes the
commandant sent in his Russians
to remove the flagpole. On enter-
ing they were met by a rush of
Chinese soldiers who attacked with
bottles and wounded four Russians.
"The Russians were then ordered
to drive the Chinese back with
their batons. In the course of this
operation a number of Chinese were
injured by batons. The flagpole
was then removed and a thorough
search made of the camp.
"About 16 of the injured Chinese
will be detained in the hospital,
while the remainder were suffering
from superficial injuries only."

Long Battle

The Russian Regiment turned
out to the scene of the argument
shortly before 10 a.m. and did not
leave the premises until after 2.30
p.m., fair indication that the battle
was something of a rather hot
affair.
Newspapermen and photographers
were not permitted inside the gates
and an air of mystery shrouded the
entire affair until 4.30 p.m. when
the Council issued its official state-
ment.
Foreign observers however, who
happened to be on Singapore Road
at the time the Russians started
removing the injured from the
camp, informed THE CHINA PRESS
last night, that three trucks were
used for this bit of transportation
work.
In the first truck to leave the
place, 37 injured soldiers were
carried out. The second truck took
12 to the hospital while six were
transported in the third truck,
making a total of 57.
The scrap between the Russians
and the soldiers started shortly
after 11 a.m. and it lasted for more
than 10 minutes. The first melee
was brought to an end in about 20
minutes but trouble still continued
in the lot.
It was not until after noon that
the affair had been placed under
control sufficiently to start sending
the injured to the police hospital.
The business of removing the
wounded had been completed by 3
p.m.
Most of the injured soldiers, suf-
fering from bumps on the head and
cuts about the face, managed to
get into the trucks under their own
steam. Seventeen were carried to
the trucks in stretchers and blank-
ets.

Ambulances Not Used

The entire affair was handled by
the Russian Regiment, which later
turned out in trucks about 10 a.m.
The police had no official informa-
tion on the affair until late in the
afternoon, and their assistance was
not requested.
The reason the wounded were
taken to the hospital in trucks and
not in emergency ambulances of the
Shanghai Fire Brigade was explain-
ed by the authorities last night as
being quite simple.
Fire brigade ambulances, during
the past two weeks, have been al-
most constantly in operation re-
moving cholera cases from the
streets and alleys of the city. This
is also the case with practically
every available rotation hospital
ambulance in the city. In many
instances, it has been even neces-
sary to use other types of vehicles
to handle the cholera cases taken
from refugee camps. Using trucks
to remove the injured soldiers was
a matter of convenience, officials
stated.
First aid was given the injured
men on the spot by Public Health
Department workers. Doctors at-
tached to the Russian Regiment
also assisted in treating the injured
Chinese soldiers after they had
taken care of the wounded Russians.
Two of the four Russians now in
the hospital last night were reported
to have been badly injured, having
sustained severe cuts about the face
and body. They will remain in the
hospital for a considerable length of
time, it was stated. The other two
probably will be able to leave with-
in a week.
Of the 16 Chinese soldiers receiv-
ing hospital treatment, five are said
to be in a serious condition. The re-
port was circulated last night that
one had died but this could not be
confirmed.
The scrap caused considerable
excitement in the Singapore Road
area. The entire population of a
large refugee camp located not far
from the concentration camp turn-
ed out in an effort to find out what
had happened, making it necessary
for the authorities to rope off the
street.
Inquiry made last night as to
what disciplinary action, if any,
might be taken against the intern-
ed Chinese soldiers, failed to pro-
duce any information on the sub-
ject. The authorities in charge of
the camp were simply not talking.

大约十分钟后，指挥官派遣其麾下的俄籍人员进入营地移除旗杆。进入时，他们遭到中国士兵的冲击，这些士兵用瓶子进行攻击，致使四名俄籍人员受伤。“随后，俄籍人员奉命使用警棍将中国士兵驱退。在此过程中，多名中国士兵被警棍击伤。随后旗杆被移除，并对营地进行了彻底搜查。
“约16名受伤的中国士兵将被留院治疗，其余人员仅受轻伤。”

激烈冲突

俄兵团于上午10点前不久抵达争执现场，直至下午2点30分后才离开，这充分表明这场冲突相当激烈。
记者和摄影师不被允许进入大门内，整个事件笼罩在神秘气氛中，直到下午4点30分工部局发布官方声明。
然而，据昨晚向《字林西报》（THE CHINA PRESS）透露的外国观察员称，当俄籍人员开始将伤者从营地运出时，他们恰好在新加坡路（Singapore Road）现场，目睹此次运输工作动用了三辆卡车。
第一辆驶离现场的卡车载有37名受伤士兵。第二辆卡车运送12人前往医院，第三辆卡车运送6人，共计57人。
俄籍人员与中国士兵之间的冲突始于上午11点后不久，持续了十多分钟。第一次混战在约20分钟内结束，但营区内仍继续发生骚乱。
直到中午过后，局势才得到足够控制，得以开始将伤者送往警务处医院。
运送伤者的工作在下午3点前完成。
大多数受伤士兵头部有肿块、面部有割伤，他们大多能自行走上卡车。另有17人是用担架和毯子抬上卡车的。

未使用救护车

整个事件由俄兵团处理，该团后来于上午10点左右出动卡车抵达现场。警方直到当天下午较晚时候才获得关于此事件的正式信息，且未收到求助请求。
当局昨晚解释称，伤者之所以用卡车而非上海救火会（Shanghai Fire Brigade）的急救救护车送往医院，原因十分简单。
在过去两周里，救火会的救护车几乎一直在不间断地运作，从城市的街道和巷弄中转运霍乱病例。市内几乎所有可用的轮班医院救护车也处于同样状态。在许多情况下，甚至不得不使用其他类型的车辆来转运从难民收容所接出的霍乱患者。官员们表示，使用卡车运送受伤士兵是出于便利考虑。
公共卫生部门的工作人员在现场对伤者进行了急救。俄兵团所属的医生在照料完受伤的俄籍人员后，也协助救治了受伤的中国士兵。
据悉，昨晚住院的四名俄籍人员中有两人伤势严重，面部和身体有多处严重割伤。据称，他们将在医院停留相当长的一段时间。另外两人可能在一周内即可出院。
在接受住院治疗的16名中国士兵中，据说有五人情况危急。昨晚流传着一人死亡的消息，但未能得到证实。
这次冲突在新加坡路地区引起了相当大的轰动。位于集中营不远处的一个大型难民收容所的全部居民都涌向现场，试图弄清发生了什么事，致使当局不得不封锁街道。
昨晚就此事询问是否会对被拘禁的中国士兵采取纪律处分，但未获得任何相关信息。负责管理营地的当局对此缄口不言。

SHANGHAI TIMES - 31.10.37.
27059

Exciting Scenes When
Chinese In Fort Make
Final Dash Over Bridge

Over 400 Men Of "Suicide Battalion" Come Into
Settlement In Early Hours Of This Morning;
Disarmed By Foreign Troops This Side

VERITABLE HAIL OF LEAD BY JAPANESE
AS RUSH TO SAFETY MADE

One of the most dramatic episodes in the history of Shang-
hai occurred here in the early hours of this morning as several
hundred soldiers from the famous "Suicide Battalion" dashed
to safety across the Tibet Road Bridge under a merciless rain
of gunfire. The whole of Yu Ya Ching Road for several blocks
into the Settlement was raked by flying bullets.

The Chinese left their post fiercely fighting their Japanese
attackers and handed over their smoking guns to British troops
stationed at the Settlement boundary. It was reported at 2
o'clock that about 400 men had crossed the bridge, and others
were still coming.

This astounding development fol-
lowed close upon the heels of a
series of stirring episodes earlier
in the evening. At an early hour
last night preparations were being
made to bring the "Doomed Bat-
talion" across Soochow Creek into
Settlement after its gallant stand
in the Joint Savings Society go-
down, where it was stranded fol-
lowing the general withdrawal
from Chapei.

To Concentration Camp

It is understood that the men will
be kept in a concentration camp
somewhere in Shanghai until the
termination of the current hostilities.

It was shortly before midnight that
the report that the famous battalion
would be brought to safety leaked
out and spread like wildfire through-
out the city. At that time it was
stated that the Chinese defenders
had agreed to give up their im-
provised fort at the urgent request
of several foreign Consular officials
in Shanghai who contended that the
hostilities centred upon the Joint
Saving Society godown were a
menace to the safety of the Settle-
ment.

Proceeding to the scene just as
the preliminary arrangements were in
full swing, a representative of "The
Shanghai Sunday Times" was witness
to the dramatic spectacle of long
lines of uniformed men being drawn
up in preparation for receiving the
battalion. Just inside the barbed
wire barrier thrown across Yu Ya
Ching Road a long line of black
marines was drawn up.

In a final check-up made last
night it was ascertained that a
number of the men, many of whom
were wounded, had been taken to
the Embankment Building.

Earlier Japanese Threat

The eyes of all Shanghai, and
perhaps the better part of the
world, were to be focused to-day on
the beleaguered "Death-with-
Honour" troops holding out in the
two godowns on North Soochow
Road against Japanese marines,
following the threat made by the
Japanese command yesterday morn-
ing to blow the Chinese out of
their stronghold, which they have
held four days.

While the announcement was
being made by Rear-Admiral Tadao
Honda, Japanese naval attache,
that, as the time limit for the with-
drawal of the Chinese unit had ex-
pired, the Japanese forces will be
compelled to resort to arms to anni-
hilate them, a letter was received
this side of the Creek from Regi-
mental Commander Hsieh Chin-
yuan, who heads the gallant defend-
ers. The letter states that the men
have no intention whatsoever of
giving up their position, but intend
to die to the last man, fighting.

All possible precautions have been
taken both by the British and
American military authorities to
protect the men occupying the
Sectors immediately facing the
godowns, which have now been
made world famous. However, it is
the British nor the Americans will
retire any distance from their out-
posts, despite the warning issued
by the Japanese.

Dangerous Positions

At the present time men of the
Royal Welch Fusiliers occupy
Blockhouse "F" which is less than
50 yards away from the Con-
tinental Bank godown on North
Soochow Road, while the U.S.
Fourth Marines are holding the
"ringside" seats to the whole affair
on the south side of the creek, west
of Yu Ya Ching Road.

While the Shanghai Gas Company
has taken all necessary precautions
against the possibility of gas tanks
on Yu Ya Ching Road being hit by
any of the large calibre missiles,
thus causing an explosion or fire,
crowds of foreigners and Chinese
continued to watch the godown and
the activity of both the Japanese
and Chinese, throughout the day
from vantage points in the Interna-
tional Settlement.

Defence Works

After three days and nights of
feverish construction, strong de-
fence works for the Joint Savings
and Trust Company godown on
North Soochow Road, the head-
quarters of the dare-to-die Chinese
lone battalion, have now almost
been completed.

This is according to Regimental
Commander Hsieh Chin-yuan, who
chose to remain with the battalion
to fight the Japanese forces to the
last drop of blood, in a letter
addressed to Lieut.-General Sun
Yuan-liang, Commander of the
88th Division.

No Publicity Stunt

The lone battalion, the letter
stresses, chose to remain behind for
the defence of Chapei merely out
of a sense of duty and patriotism,
and not for the sake of publicity.

"Up till now," Commander Hsieh
states, "I have not given any press
interview nor made any demands
on the public. Whatever has
been printed in the press emanates
purely from outside."

Night and day, the letter says,
members of the battalion have been
thinking of nothing else but the
determination to die to the last
man, in order to accomplish their
mission.

"Death is not an important issue,"
the letter continues, "but we wish
to inform you that before our mis-
sion is accomplished we will not
make our sacrifices lightly."

Speculation has been rife for the
past two days as to what method
the Japanese will employ in order
to get the Chinese out and take
over the two godowns, the last re-
maining stronghold of the Chinese
in Chapei. It is generally believed
that the Japanese will bomb the
two godowns; on the other hand
this method is likely to bring com-
plications in view of the close prox-
imity of the foreign sectors.

With several houses some distance
to the north-west of the godowns
having been set on fire yesterday
and having burned out by nightfall
it is believed that the Japanese
have been clearing a view from
some distance in order to bring
howitzers into action against the
isolated unit in the godowns.

Complete destruction of the go-
downs is neither the object of the
Chinese nor the Japanese as large
quantities of rice and grain are
stored in them.

French Mortars Fired

Trench mortars were brought in-
to action by the Japanese yester-
day morning, considerable damage
to the western wall of the Joint
Savings Society Godown being done
by the firing. Several shells fell on
North Soochow Road not far from
Blockhouse "F". Chinese defenders,
however, had the better of the Jap-
anese at closer quarters, when they
fired on the Japanese marines walk-
ing on the roof of an adjoining go-
down, which is considerable lower
than the Joint Savings Society Go-
down building.

"Our godown is glorified by the
presence of the lone Chinese batta-
lion, who are resolved to fight to
the last. We will never regret even
if the structure should be complete-
ly destroyed by the Japanese," stat-
ed Mr. Y. M. Chien, assistant gen-
eral manager of the Joint Savings
Society, commenting on the situa-
tion. The name of the godown, he
added, would go on record with
the battalion for their epic strug-
gle against stupendous odds.

Japanese Statement

The Japanese armed forces have
completed preparations for dis-
lodging Chinese troops from their
stronghold in the Joint Savings
Society's godown, on North Soo-
chow Road, Rear-Admiral Tadao
Honda, naval attache to the Japan-
ese Embassy, announced yesterday
morning.

Residents living in proximity to
the godown were asked by the
officer to take all necessary pre-
cautions to safeguard themselves
during the Japanese attack.

"If the Chinese soldiers entrench-
ed in the godown continue their
resistance," Rear-Admiral Honda's
prepared statement read, "we shall
be forced to resort to arms to an-
nihilate them.

《上海泰晤士报》 - 1937年10月31日。
27059

中国守军在堡垒中发起最后冲锋越过桥梁时的惊险场面

“敢死队”四百余名官兵于今日凌晨进入租界；
在此一侧被外国军队解除武装

日军在守军冲向安全地带时倾泻了真正的弹雨

上海历史上最富戏剧性的一幕之一发生于今日凌晨，数百名来自著名的“敢死队”的士兵在无情的枪林弹雨中冲过西藏路桥，奔向安全地带。数条街区内的虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）直至租界内部，均遭到飞射子弹的扫射。

中国守军在与日本进攻者激烈交火后撤离阵地，并将尚有余温的枪支交给驻扎在租界边界的英军。据凌晨2时报告，约有400人已过桥，且仍有后续人员陆续到来。

这一惊人进展紧随当晚早些时候一系列激动人心的事件之后。昨夜初，人们正着手准备将这支“注定牺牲的营”在联合储蓄会仓库英勇坚守后，从闸北全面撤退而被困的局面中解救出来，渡过苏州河进入租界。

送往集中营

据悉，这些士兵将被关押在上海某处的集中营内，直至当前敌对行动结束。

就在午夜前不久，关于这支著名部队将被转移至安全地带的消息泄露出来，并如野火般传遍全市。当时称，中国守军已同意放弃其临时构筑的堡垒，这是应上海几位外国领事官员的紧急请求而作出的决定，这些官员认为，围绕联合储蓄会仓库的战斗对租界的安全构成了威胁。

就在初步安排紧锣密鼓地进行之际，《上海星期泰晤士报》的一名代表赶赴现场，目睹了身着制服的人员排成长列、准备接收该营的戏剧性场面。在横跨虞洽卿路设置的铁丝网屏障内侧，一长列黑衣海军陆战队员整齐列队。

在昨夜进行的最后一次核查中，确认包括许多伤员在内的一部分士兵已被送往外滩大楼（Embankment Building）。

日军此前的威胁

今天，全上海乃至世界大部分地区的目光都聚焦在被围困的“光荣赴死”部队身上，他们在北苏州路的两座仓库中坚守，对抗日本海军陆战队。此前，日军指挥部于昨天上午发出威胁，要将中国军队从其已坚守四天的据点中炸出。

就在日本海军武官本田忠雄少将（Rear-Admiral Tadao Honda）宣布，鉴于中国部队撤离的时限已过，日军将被迫诉诸武力将其歼灭之时，苏州河此侧收到了率领这支英勇守军的团谢晋元指挥官（Regimental Commander Hsieh Chin-yuan）的来信。信中指出，士兵们绝无放弃阵地的意图，而是打算战斗至最后一人，誓死不屈。

英美军事当局均已采取一切可能的预防措施，以保护那些占据正对仓库区域的人员，这些仓库如今已闻名世界。然而，尽管日军发出警告，无论是英军还是美军都不会从他们的前哨阵地后退任何距离。

危险的位置

目前，皇家威尔士燧发枪团（Royal Welch Fusiliers）的士兵占据着“F”号碉堡，该处距离北苏州路的大陆银行仓库不到50码；而美国海军陆战队第四团则占据了整个事件的“前排座位”，位于苏州河南岸、虞洽卿路以西。

虽然上海煤气公司已采取一切必要预防措施，以防虞洽卿路上的储气罐被任何大口径炮弹击中从而引发爆炸或火灾，但全天仍有大批外国人和中国人从公共租界内的有利位置持续观察仓库以及中日双方的活动。

防御工事

经过三天三夜的紧张施工，位于北苏州路的联合储蓄信托公司仓库——即中国孤军“敢死队”总部——的坚固防御工事现已基本完工。

这是根据谢晋元团长在致第八十八师师长孙元良中将（Lieut.-General Sun Yuan-liang）的信中所述，谢团长选择留在军中，与日军血战到底。

并非宣传噱头

信中强调，孤军选择留下保卫闸北，仅仅是出于责任感和爱国心，而非为了宣传。

谢团长表示：“截至目前，我未接受任何媒体采访，也未向公众提出任何要求。见诸报端的内容纯属外界自发传播。”

信中说，全营官兵日夜所思唯有完成使命的决心，即战斗至最后一人。

信中还写道：“死亡并非重要问题，但我们希望告知您，在使命完成之前，我们不会轻言牺牲。”

过去两天，关于日军将采用何种方法将中国军队赶出并接管这两座仓库——中国在闸北最后的据点——的猜测甚嚣尘上。普遍相信日军将轰炸这两座仓库；另一方面，鉴于其与外国防区近在咫尺，这种方法可能会带来复杂局面。

由于仓库西北方向几栋房屋于昨日被点燃并在夜幕降临时烧毁，人们认为日军正在清理一定距离内的视野，以便调动榴弹炮攻击仓库中的孤立部队。

彻底摧毁仓库既非中方也非日方的目标，因为其中储存着大量大米和谷物。

法军迫击炮开火

日军于昨天上午投入使用了战壕迫击炮，对联合储蓄会仓库的西墙造成了相当程度的破坏。几发炮弹落在离“F”号碉堡不远的北苏州路上。然而，中国守军在近距离战斗中优于日军，他们向走在相邻仓库屋顶上的日本海军陆战队员开火，该相邻仓库比联合储蓄会仓库建筑低得多。

联合储蓄会副总经理钱新之先生（Mr. Y. M. Chien）在评论局势时表示：“孤军中国营的存在使我们的仓库增光添彩，他们决心战斗到底。即使建筑结构被日军完全摧毁，我们也绝不后悔。”他补充说，该仓库的名字将因该营在巨大劣势下的史诗般斗争而载入史册。

日军声明

日本驻华大使馆海军武官本田忠雄少将于昨天上午宣布，日军已完成准备，将把中国军队从其在北苏州路联合储蓄会仓库的据点中驱逐出去。

该军官要求居住在仓库附近的居民在日军进攻期间采取一切必要措施保护自己。

本田少将的预备声明称：“如果固守在仓库内的中国士兵继续抵抗，我们将被迫诉诸武力将其歼灭。

"As is generally known, a part of
the Chinese troops whose retreat
from Chapei was cut off by the
Special Naval Landing Party sought
refuge in the godown.
"Moved by our desire to spare
the lives of the Chinese soldiers
from the standpoints of humanity
and Bushido on the one hand, and
on the other hand to avoid com-
plications arising out of the
geographical position of the godown,
the Naval Landing Party had taken
every possible step to persuade the
Chinese to leave the godown.
"Nevertheless, the Chinese unit
showed no signs of accepting our
generous and amicable proposal in
the ecstasy of being hailed as
'national heroes.'
Plans Completed
"The Special Naval Landing
Party of the Imperial Navy com-
pleted its preparations to dislodge
the Chinese from their position on
Thursday.
"The Naval Landing Party
realizes that the attack on the go-
down, in view of its proximity to
the British and American defence
sectors, might result in complica-
tions.
"It must be realized by all, how-
ever, that Japan cannot delay
the attack indefinitely. Now the
time limit set by us for the with-
drawal of the Chinese has expired.
"Should they continue to resist
our bluejackets and hold their
present position, the Japanese forces
will be compelled to resort to arms
to annihilate them.
"The residents in the area ad-
jacent to the godown are urged to
take all necessary precautions to
safeguard themselves during the
Japanese attack."
Courageous Girl Guide
It was revealed here last night,
according to the "Lih Pao," that the
new Chinese flag on the godowns,
a gift from the Shanghai Civic
Association, was "smuggled" into the
headquarters of the dare-to-die
battalion by a girl scout, Miss Yang
Hui-min, on Thursday night.
While details were not given as to
how she did it, her courageous act
was reported to have aroused city-
wide admiration.
Aged 24 and a native of Chinkiang,
Miss Yang enrolled as a girl scout
shortly after the outbreak of the
Shanghai hostilities. During the
Manchurian crisis, she joined a
Chinese volunteer corps in the
north-east, where she had been
doing publicity work for more than
two years.

计划已完成
“帝国海军特别海军陆战队已于周四完成将中国人从其阵地驱逐出去的准备工作。

“然而，所有人都必须认识到，日本不能无限期推迟攻击。现在我们设定的中国军队撤离时限已过。
“如果他们继续抵抗我们的水兵并坚守现有阵地，日军将被迫诉诸武力将其歼灭。
“敦促仓库邻近地区的居民在日军进攻期间采取一切必要措施保护自己。”
勇敢的女童子军

据《立报》昨晚披露，仓库上悬挂的新中国国旗——由上海市市民协会赠送——是由一名女童子军杨惠敏小姐（Miss Yang Hui-min）于周四晚上“偷运”进敢死队总部的。

虽然未透露她是如何做到的细节，但据报道，她的勇敢行为引起了全市的钦佩。

杨小姐现年24岁，镇江人，在上海战事爆发后不久便注册成为女童子军。在满洲危机期间，她加入了东北的一支中国志愿队，在那里从事宣传工作已有两年多。

After Heavy Artillery Battle

Heavy Fighting Preludes Withdrawal; Japanese
Train Artillery Directly On Building;
British Offer Safe Conduct

The Chinese "doomed battalion" in the Joint Savings Society godown on North Thibet Road evacuated into the Settlement at an early hour this morning.

After resisting everything the Japanese Navy had to offer for nearly four days, members of the battalion began to trickle out after mid-night in small parties. By 2 o'clock this morning, more than 360 had been conducted to the Embankment Building by the British authorities.

Long before the last man had evacuated, Japanese guns had fired the top floor of the main godown. The field pieces were placed between the two godowns and were pointed at the top stories less than 40 yards from the big windows.

Shot and shell flew in all directions from 11 p.m. up until the time that the men decided definitely to withdraw. Residents living in the Louza District thought hell itself had turned loose.

It was reported that the Chinese had decided upon this action after representations had been made by foreign authorities asking them to enter the Settlement on the grounds that their presence in the Joint Savings Society godown was seriously endangering areas south of Soochow Creek.

Danger Of Explosion

It was further stated that these representations were made when officials of the Shanghai Gas Company took alarm at the statement made by the Japanese yesterday that arrangements for launching a heavy offensive against the godown had been undertaken.

The possibility of a badly aimed Japanese aerial bomb was considered so great that the gas tank might be blown up with severe damage to the entire district. The tank is located just across Yu Ya Ching Road bridge on the south side of the creek.

Rapidly becoming as famous as the valiant 600 horsemen of Crimean War fame, immortalized by Lord Alfred Tennyson in "The Charge of the Light Brigade," the "doomed battalion" of the crack 88th Division grimly continued to hold out yesterday against the efforts of the Japanese navy to dislodge it and remove the Chinese flag from Chapei.

Throughout the day, the Japanese kept up constant machine-gun fire against the Joint Savings Society godown on the corner of North Thibet and North Soochow Roads in Chapei. Rifle-grenades were also used while fieldpieces west of the Continental Bank godown did a bit of shelling but to little avail.

Strong defense works for the godown had been completed by the defending Chinese troops, according to a letter passed out of the place by Colonel Hsieh Chin-yuan, commanding the detachment, and addressed to Lt.-Gen. Sun Yuan-liang, commander of the 88th Division. The letter, dated October 29, sheds much light hitherto undisclosed on the drama of gallantry and bravery now being enacted before the eyes of Shanghai's millions.

80 Japanese Killed

On October 27, the letter reports, the Japanese in an unsuccessful attempt to storm the godown, suffered heavy casualties, leaving more than 80 dead bodies behind them.

"Shortly after 6 a.m. on October 28," Colonel Hsieh states, "I shot dead two Japanese soldiers myself." He added that the lone battalion chose to remain behind for the defense of Chapei merely out of a sense of duty and patriotism and not for the sake of publicity.

In another letter to Major-General Feng Sheng-fah, deputy commander of the 88th, Colonel Hsieh says that for the shedding of their blood they must demand a costly price from the Japanese.

Another letter which has a bearing on the situation is one from Lt.-Gen. Sun, written to Mr. Tu Yueh-sen, prominent banker and chairman of the Chinese Residents Civic Association.

General Sun expressed appreciation to the public for their great interest shown in the welfare of the lone battalion and for the large quantities of foodstuffs and other things presented to them.

The people, however, were asked not to continue sending things to the beleaguered warriors, because so many things are easily perishable, and besides, they have enough food stores to hold out for a long time.

Give To Liberty Bonds

Money intended for the purpose, in Commander Sun's opinion, should be devoted to the purchase of Liberty Bonds or donated toward the fund for providing pensions for the families of officers and soldiers killed during the hostilities.

"Our godown is glorified by the presence of the lone Chinese battalion which is resolved to fight to the last. We will never regret the loss, even if the structure should be completely destroyed by the Japanese."

This statement was made yesterday by Mr. Y. M. Chien, assistant general manager of the Joint Savings Society, in connection with the occupation of the bank's warehouse by the "doomed battalion."

"Chinese Who Won't Get Out"

The name of the godown, said Mr. Chien, would go on record with the battalion for their epic struggle against stupendous odds.

The presence of the battalion in the godown brought forth a variety of statements from the Japanese. Two days ago, they were referred to as "stragglers" yesterday they were officially known in Japanese circles as the "Chinese in the godown who won't get out."

Another Chinese Flag Flying

Instead of one, two Chinese flags were flying yesterday from two godowns.

The second flag, like the first one, was "smuggled" into the Chinese citadel.

During the four days the lone battalion kept the Japanese at bay, attention of the entire world was attracted to the gallant stand made by the Chinese. Foreign observers considered it another Alcazar but forgot that this fortress had glass windows.

On the other hand the moral effect which the episode had was not underestimated. Sooner or later, it was generally agreed that the overwhelming force of enemy mechanized units or aircraft would achieve their objective, but because the defenders were willing to flout this very force, it made their stand even the more impressive.

《字林西报》 - 1937年10月31日。
27050

中国营
撤离北西藏路仓库

激烈炮战后顶层起火

撤退前激战；日军火炮直接瞄准大楼；
英方提供安全通行保证

驻守于北西藏路四行联合准备库（Joint Savings Society godown）的中国“孤军营”于今日凌晨撤入租界。

在抵挡日本海军近四天的所有攻势后，该营官兵于午夜过后开始分批零星撤出。截至今日凌晨2时，已有超过360人由英国当局护送至河滨大厦（Embankment Building）。

在最后一名士兵撤离之前很久，日军火炮就已击中了主仓库的顶层。野战炮被部署在两栋仓库之间，炮口直指距大窗户不到40码的顶层楼层。

从晚上11点直到士兵们决定坚决撤退之时，枪弹四处横飞。居住在老闸区（Louza District）的居民以为地狱之门大开。

据报道，在外方当局以中国军队驻守四行联合准备库严重危及苏州河南岸地区为由，要求他们进入租界并进行交涉后，中方决定了这一行动。

爆炸危险

另有消息称，当上海煤气公司官员对日军昨日发表的关于已着手安排对该仓库发动猛烈进攻的声明感到惊恐时，便提出了上述交涉。

日军航空炸弹瞄准失误的可能性极大，可能导致煤气罐爆炸，从而对整个地区造成严重破坏。该煤气罐位于苏州河南岸，就在虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）桥对面。

这支隶属于精锐第八十八师的“孤军营”，其名声迅速媲美克里米亚战争中因阿尔弗雷德·丁尼生勋爵在《轻骑兵冲锋》一诗中使其不朽的六百勇士，昨日仍顽强坚守，抵抗日本海军将其驱逐并移除闸北中国国旗的努力。

整天，日军持续用机枪扫射位于闸北北西藏路与北苏州路交界处的四行联合准备库。期间还使用了步枪榴弹，而位于大陆银行仓库西侧的野战炮也进行了一些炮击，但收效甚微。

据该分队指挥官谢晋元团长写给第八十八师师长孙元良中将的一封信透露，防守的中国军队已完成仓库的坚固防御工事。这封日期为10月29日的信件，揭示了目前在上海数百万民众眼前上演的英勇壮烈戏剧中此前未披露的大量细节。

80名日军毙命

信中报告称，10月27日，日军在试图强攻仓库未果的行动中遭受重大伤亡，留下了80多具尸体。

谢团长称：“10月28日早上6点后不久，我亲自击毙了两名日本士兵。”他补充说，该孤军选择留守保卫闸北，纯粹是出于责任感和爱国心，而非为了博取名声。

在给第八十八师副师长冯圣法少将的另一封信中，谢团长表示，既然流了血，就必须向日本人索取高昂的代价。

另一封与局势有关的信件是孙元良中将写给著名银行家、上海市民协会主席杜月笙先生的。

孙将军对公众对孤军营福祉表现出的极大兴趣，以及向他们赠送的大量食品和其他物资表示感谢。

然而，他请求民众不要再向被围困的战士运送物资，因为许多物品容易腐烂，此外，他们拥有足够的粮食储备以长期坚守。

购买救国公债

孙指挥官认为，原本打算用于此目的的资金，应用于购买救国公债，或捐赠给为阵亡军官和士兵家属提供抚恤金的基金。

“我们的仓库因这支决心战斗到最后一刻的中国孤军营的存在而增光添彩。即使建筑物被日军完全摧毁，我们也绝不后悔损失。”

四行联合准备库副总经理钱新之（Y. M. Chien）先生昨日就“孤军营”占领银行仓库一事发表了上述声明。

“不肯撤出的中国人”

钱先生称，该仓库的名字将因该营在巨大劣势下的史诗般抗争而与这支队伍一起载入史册。

孤军营驻扎在仓库内，引来了日方的各种说法。两天前，他们被称为“散兵游勇”；昨天，他们在日本圈子里被正式称为“仓库里不肯撤出的中国人”。

又一面中国国旗升起

昨天，两面中国国旗而非一面，在两栋仓库上空飘扬。

第二面旗帜像第一面一样，是被“偷运”进中国堡垒的。

在这四天里，孤军营挡住了日军，全世界的目光都集中在中国人的英勇坚守上。外国观察家认为这是另一个阿尔卡萨城堡（Alcazar），但忘记了这座堡垒有着玻璃窗。

另一方面，这一事件产生的道德影响并未被低估。人们普遍认为，敌方机械化部队或飞机的压倒性力量迟早会实现其目标，但由于守军愿意蔑视这种力量，这使得他们的坚守更加令人印象深刻。

august 19, 1939.

TAIRIKU SHIMPO

*INTERNED CHINESE SOLDIERS IN THE FOREIGN SETTLEMENTS
SHOULD BE HANDED OVER TO JAPANESE ARMY*

The Tairiku Shimpo publishes
the following comments:-
We have raised a question about
the feeding of the interned Chinese soldiers at the expense
of the S.M.C. In this connection Commander Hsia of the
interned soldiers has published a declaration refuting our
protest.
In his declaration Commander
Hsia maintains that the soldiers had surrendered voluntarily
in compliance with a decision reached by the Consular Body
in order to remove the danger to life and property in the
Foreign Settlements. He also protests against the treatment
of the interned soldiers.
In connection with the question
of expenses, Commander Hsia states that between October, 1937
and November, 1938, local relief associations had been paying
for their upkeep and between December, 1938 and August this
year the S.M.C. had advanced $40,500 for this purpose, but
against this the Chungking Government has already paid
$43,600 to the S.M.C. Therefore, there is still a balance
of $3,100 in the hands of the S.M.C.
We do not know whether Hsia's
statement is true or not, however, we expect that the S.M.C.
will make an explanation regarding the matter.
The source of the funds for the
upkeep of the interned soldiers is a secondary question.
What we demand is that all interned soldiers be handed over
to the Japanese authorities as they are in an area under
the control of the Japanese army.
Besides the interned soldiers
from the Four Banks' godown, the records of other soldiers
who had entered the Foreign Settlements and the arms seized
from them should also be handed over to the Japanese
authorities. According to an investigation made, about 7,000
soldiers have entered the foreign areas.
The authorities of the Foreign
Settlements may attempt to hide the presence of these
soldiers on the ground that the Foreign Settlements constitute
neutral ground, but we claim that as the foreign areas are
in an occupied area, we cannot recognize their neutrality.
Last year the interned soldiers
in the Kiaochow Road Camp attempted to hoist the Kuomintang
flag and caused serious trouble with the Russian guards,
resulting in bloodshed. They are now reported to be
attempting to regain their freedom as quickly as possible.
They are under the protection of the S.M.C. yet they have
adopted a hostile attitude towards Japan.
There is stronger ground for the
handing over of the interned soldiers than for the extradition
of the four offenders in Tientsin.

1939年8月19日。

《大陆新报》

*应将在公共租界内被拘禁的中国士兵移交给日本军队*

《大陆新报》发表如下评论：-

我们就由工部局承担费用供养被拘禁中国士兵一事提出了质疑。对此，被拘禁士兵的指挥官夏某（Hsia）发表声明，反驳我们的抗议。

在其声明中，夏指挥官坚称，士兵们是根据领事团为消除公共租界内生命财产危险而达成的决定，自愿投降的。他还对被拘禁士兵所受的待遇提出抗议。

关于费用问题，夏指挥官称，1937年10月至1938年11月期间，当地救济团体一直支付他们的给养费用；而从1938年12月至今年8月，工部局为此垫付了40,500美元，但对此重庆政府已向工部局支付了43,600美元。因此，工部局手中仍有3,100美元的余额。

我们不知夏某的陈述是否属实，但我们期望工部局就此事项作出解释。

被拘禁士兵给养资金的来源是次要问题。我们要求的是，将所有被拘禁士兵移交给日本当局，因为他们处于日本军队控制的区域内。

除了来自四行仓库的被拘禁士兵外，其他进入公共租界的士兵的记录以及从他们那里缴获的武器也应移交给日本当局。据调查，约有7,000名士兵进入了外侨区域。

公共租界当局可能会以公共租界构成中立地带为由，试图隐瞒这些士兵的存在，但我们声称，由于外侨区域位于占领区内，我们不能承认其中立性。

去年，胶州路营房内的被拘禁士兵试图悬挂国民党旗，并与俄国守卫发生严重冲突，导致流血事件。据报道，他们现在正试图尽快重获自由。他们虽受工部局保护，却对日本采取敌对态度。

移交被拘禁士兵的理由比引渡天津四名罪犯的理由更为充分。

pages.en:
August 16, 1939.

TAIRIKU SHIMPO

"JAPANESE MILITARY AUTHORITIES AND THE CHINESE
INTERNED SOLDIERS"

The 230 odd Chinese soldiers of
the 88th Division of the National Government's Army have
been interned in the camp on Kiaochow Road since their
surrender to the British Defence Force. As remarked yesterday
by this paper, these soldiers have been and are still being
kept at the expense of the S.M.C. since the withdrawal of
the National Government from Nanking.
Japan is one of the member Powers
reponsible for the International Settlement; furthermore
Shanghai lies in the area under the occupation of the Japanese
army. We cannot overlook the fact that these enemy soldiers,
who had fought our soldiers in Shanghai, are now being
protected and fed by the S.M.C. It is reported that
the Japanese military authorities will request the S.M.C.
to hand over the interned soldiers on the following grounds:-
1) From the viewpoint of the removal of anti-Japanese
elements, the question of the upkeep of interned soldiers
by the S.M.C. cannot be overlooked as the International
Settlement lies in an occupied area and has no neutrality.
2) In the Tientsin issue, the British authorities have
already promised to hand over the four offenders responsible
for the murder of the Customs Commissioner; therefore, there
is no reason for the Municipal authorities here to refuse
to hand over the interned soldiers to Japan as she is one
of the member Powers interested in Municipal affairs.
3) Should the S.M.C. reject the demand to hand over
the interned soldiers, it will be regarded as an organ of
the Chungking Government and not as an international
organization for it has violated its international character.
Various quarters are hoping that the Japanese military
authorities will take strong measures in this connection.
Besides the above issue, another
question has been raised about the attitude of the S.M.C.
towards the large number of Chinese soldiers who entered
the International Settlement during the local hostilities.
It is believed that about 8,000 soldiers had entered the
Foreign Settlements from Chapei and Nantao during the three
months of local hostilities and were liberated after they
had been disarmed by the authorities. Naturally the
authorities concerned must have kept records of the number
of persons and the quantity of arms surrendered. These
records must be handed to the Japanese authorities to be
used in dealing with the Foreign Settlements which lies in
occupied area.
Where these disarmed soldiers
are now and what they are doing, it is not known, but most
of them are believed to be engaged in anti-Japanese activities.
It is reported that arms of various descriptions are being
sold in the Foreign Settlements at cheap prices. This
would seem to suggest that the arms seized from interned
soldiers by the Settlement authorities are being handed out
to the public. The authorities of the Foreign Settlements,
by refusing to hand over to the Japanese authorities the
records of the number of interned soldiers and of the arms
seized from them, are demonstrating a hostile attitude. The
Japanese military authorities are paying close attention to
these points.

1939年8月16日。

《大陆新报》

“日本军方与中国被拘禁士兵”

国民政府军队第八十八师的230余名中国士兵自向英国防卫部队投降以来，一直被拘禁在胶州路的营房内。正如本报昨日所述，自国民政府撤离南京以来，这些士兵一直并由工部局出资供养。

日本是负责国际租界的成员国之一；此外，上海位于日本军队占领区内。我们不能忽视这样一个事实：这些曾在上海与我军作战的敌军士兵，现在正受到工部局的保护和供养。据悉，日本军方将基于以下理由要求工部局移交被拘禁士兵：-

1) 从清除反日分子的角度来看，工部局供养被拘禁士兵的问题不容忽视，因为国际租界位于占领区内，不具有中立性。

2) 在天津事件中，英国当局已承诺移交对谋杀海关专员负责的四名罪犯；因此，这里的市政当局没有理由拒绝将被拘禁士兵移交给作为关心市政事务的成员国之一的日本。

3) 如果工部局拒绝移交被拘禁士兵的要求，它将被视为重庆政府的机构，而非国际组织，因为它违反了其国际性质。

各界希望日本军方在此问题上采取强硬措施。

除上述问题外，还有人提出了关于工部局对在本地敌对行动期间进入国际租界的大量中国士兵的态度问题。据信，在本地敌对行动的三个月期间，约有8,000名士兵从闸北和南市进入外侨区域，并在被当局解除武装后获释。当然，有关当局一定保留了人数和缴获武器数量的记录。这些记录必须移交给日本当局，用于处理位于占领区内的外侨区域事务。

这些被解除武装的士兵现在何处以及正在做什么，尚不清楚，但据信大多数人正从事反日活动。据报道，各种类型的武器正在外侨区域以低价出售。这似乎表明，租界当局从被拘禁士兵那里缴获的武器正在分发给公众。外侨区域当局拒绝向日本当局移交被拘禁士兵人数及从他们那里缴获武器的记录，表现出一种敌对态度。日本军方正密切关注这些要点。

pages.en:
August 15, 1939.

TAIRIKU SHIMPO

"S.M.C., BY FEEDING AND PROTECTING INTERNED CHINESE
SOLDIERS FROM THE FOUR BANKS GODOWN, DEMONSTRATES
ITS HOSTILE ATTITUDE"

About 230 Chinese soldiers under
the command of Hsia Poo Yuan of the 88th Division of the
Central Government army, who took up a position in the
Four Banks Godown to offer resistance to our army during
the local hostilities, finally surrendered to the British
Defence Force and since then they have been interned in
a camp at the corner of Kiaochow Road and Singapore Road.
On August 13, 1938, the first
anniversary of the outbreak of the Shanghai hostilities,
these soldiers had some trouble with the Russian guards
of the camp over an attempt to hoist the Kuomintang flag
over the camp. As a result of the trouble, two of
the soldiers were killed. On the anniversary this year,
these soldiers were quiet.
However, some question has been
raised over the feeding of the interned soldiers at the
expense of the S.M.C.
When the soldiers surrendered
to the British Defence Force it was reported that the
National Government would send money for their upkeep.
This was done for only 2 or 3 months and was discontinued
after the fall of Nanking. The Chungking Government
is not now in a position to send money to Shanghai. In
spite of this, the S.M.C. is advancing funds for their
food in the belief that the National Government will
repay the money.
We are concerned over the action
of the S.M.C. in feeding these soldiers for an unknown
period. The Japanese residents know that the S.M.C. is
officially giving protection to the interned soldiers in
the International Settlement which lies in an area under
the control of the Japanese army and they are highly
indignant over the matter. They express a hope that
their authorities in Shanghai will take proper steps.
It is reported that a number of
Japanese residents are suggesting the non-payment of the
Municipal rate as a demonstration against the hostile
attitude of the S.M.C. which is feeding the soldiers with
funds collected partly from Japanese residents in the form
of Municipal rates. Developments in the affair will
be watched with close attention.
pages.zh:
1939年8月15日。

《大陆新报》

“工部局通过供养和保护四行仓库被拘禁的中国士兵，显示其敌对态度”

在局部冲突期间，中央政府军第88师夏朴元（Hsia Poo Yuan，音译）指挥下的约230名中国士兵占据四行仓库阵地以抵抗我军，最终向英国防卫队投降，此后他们一直被拘禁在胶州路与新加坡路拐角处的一个营地中。1938年8月13日，即上海战事爆发一周年之际，这些士兵因试图在营地升起国民党旗帜而与营地俄籍守卫发生纠纷。作为纠纷的结果，两名士兵被杀。在今年的纪念日，这些士兵保持安静。

然而，有人对由工部局出资供养被拘禁士兵一事提出质疑。
当士兵们向英国防卫队投降时，据报道国民政府将汇款供其维持生活。此举仅持续了两三个月，在南京沦陷后便停止了。重庆政府目前无力向上海汇款。尽管如此，工部局仍垫付他们的伙食费，相信国民政府会偿还这笔款项。

我们对工部局在未知期限内供养这些士兵的行为表示关切。日本侨民知道，工部局正式保护位于日军控制区域内的国际租界中的被拘禁士兵，他们对此事极为愤慨。他们希望其在上海的当局采取适当措施。
据报道，许多日本侨民建议拒缴市政捐，以此抗议工部局的敌对态度，因为工部局是用包括从日本侨民处收取的市政捐在内的资金来供养士兵的。我们将密切关注此事的事态发展。

October 27, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Ta Mei Pao, Shun Pao, Chinese-American Daily News :-

LONE BATTALION ANNIVERSARY

Yesterday was the second anniversary of the
heroic defence of the Joint Savings Bank Godown in Chapei
by the Lone Battalion of the 88th Division. On that day
in 1937, the 400 men of the 88th Division put up a
courageous stand at the godown despite the heavy
bombardment. Their heroic spirit aroused world-wide
admiration. On the advice of the authorities of the
Settlement who were solicitous for the safety of the
Settlement, these 400 brave defenders retreated against
their wish into the Settlement and have since been
interned at the Kiaochow Road Camp.
A service to celebrate the anniversary was
held at 3 p.m. yesterday in the presence of 100
representatives of local public bodies.
In the course of a speech, Colonel Zia Tsing-
yuan (謝晉元), who presided over the ceremony, said:
"To-day's anniversary has a very significant meaning;
it should enable us to reflect on the past and encourage
us in the future. The recent unprecedented victory
scored by us in North Hunan tells us that the Japanese
are now nearing the end of their resources; it also
gives us an assurance for final victory. At this time
when the war of resistance has reached its most critical
phase, the Chinese people, unless they are willing to be
slaves, should render to the nation more strenuous
services financially or otherwise.
"It was Japan's aggression that caused China
to start the present war of resistance. For this reason,
there is no way open to the Chinese people. We are
fighting to ensure the complete safety of the sovereign
and territorial integrity of the country and to crush
Japan's ambitious designs for the subjugation of China."

《大美报》、《申报》、《中美日报》：

孤军周年纪念

昨天是第88师孤军在闸北四行储蓄会仓库英勇防御的两周年纪念日。1937年的那一天，第88师的400名官兵在猛烈炮火下于仓库进行了勇敢的坚守。他们的英雄气概赢得了全世界的钦佩。出于对租界安全的关切，租界当局建议这400名勇敢的保护者违背意愿撤入租界，此后他们一直被拘禁在胶州路营地。

昨天下午3点，在当地公共团体100名代表的出席下，举行了纪念周年的仪式。
主持仪式的谢晋元上校在演讲中说：“今天的周年纪念具有非常重大的意义；它应使我们反思过去，并激励我们面向未来。最近我们在湘北取得的空前胜利告诉我们，日本人现在已接近资源枯竭；这也给了我们要取得最终胜利的信心。在抗战达到最关键时刻的此时，中国人民除非愿意做奴隶，否则应在财政或其他方面为国家提供更艰巨的服务。

“正是日本的侵略导致中国开始了目前的抗战。因此，中国人民别无选择。我们战斗是为了确保国家主权和领土完整的绝对安全，并粉碎日本征服中国的野心阴谋。”

January 17, 1939. Morning Translation.

Chinese American Daily News and other local newspapers:

THE PAY AND RATIONS OF THE LONE BATTALION

In connection with the report published by the "Ta Mei Pao" (大美報) of January 16 on the pay and rations of the Lone Battalion in the Kiaochow Road Park, the entire body of officers and men of the Battalion have issued the following important statements:-

"We were greatly surprised to read in the 'Ta Mei Pao' on January 16 a report as well as a letter said to have been issued by the Battalion of the 88th Division, on the pay and rations of our Battalion.

"It is to be noted that since our withdrawal from the Joint Savings Society Godown last year under the lead of Colonel Zia Tsing-yuan (謝晉元), we have remained in Shanghai and have gone through many hardships. During the past year, Colonel Zia has been much exhausted through giving instructions to members of the Battalion and in dealing with various matters.

"The letter published by the 'Ta Mei Pao' was not issued by the officers and men of our Battalion. It was written with the object of injuring the reputation of the Lone Battalion and alienating the confidence of the people. Apart from denying the statements in the letter, we hereby inform the public of the circumstances surrounding the matter:-

1) The National Government issued a reward of $3,000 to the Lone Battalion. This money was handed to company commanders by Colonel Zia to be distributed, according to rank, among the soldiers.

2) The Lone Battalion received pay and rations for only two months, because the other two months' pay and rations had not been issued for certain reasons. Colonel Zia has repeatedly urged the issue of this money. These are the facts and can be proved by an investigation.

3) The subscriptions received by the Lone Battalion have been openly announced in newspapers by Colonel Zia. They have been entered in books, even if the amount is only one cent.

"Being a revolutionary soldier, Colonel Zia is honest. The officers and men of our Battalion are of the opinion that the person responsible for the issue of the letter to the 'Ta Mei Pao' must have been made use of by certain persons for some ulterior motive, thereby injuring the glorious history of our Lone Battalion and indirectly harming the reputation of the nation.

"With a view to exposing the sinister plans of traitorous elements, we hereby issue this statement for public information."

针对《大美报》1月16日发表的关于胶州路公园孤军薪饷和口粮的报道，孤军全体官兵发表了以下重要声明：

“我们惊讶地读到，《大美报》1月16日刊登了一篇报道以及一封据称由第88师某营发出的关于我营薪饷和口粮的信。

“值得注意的是，自去年在谢晋元上校率领下从四行储蓄会仓库撤退以来，我们一直留在上海，经历了许多艰难困苦。在过去的一年里，谢上校因指导营内成员和处理各种事务而疲惫不堪。

“《大美报》刊登的信件并非由我营官兵发出。其撰写目的是损害孤军的声誉并离间民众的信任。除了否认信中的陈述外，我们特此向公众通报此事的相关情况：

1) 国民政府向孤军颁发了3,000元奖金。这笔钱由谢上校交给连长，按军衔分发给士兵。

2) 孤军只收到了两个月的薪饷和口粮，因为另外两个月的薪饷和口粮因某些原因未发放。谢上校已多次催促发放这笔款项。这些都是事实，可以通过调查证明。

3) 孤军收到的捐款已由谢上校在报纸上公开公布。即使金额只有一分钱，也已记入账册。

“作为一名革命军人，谢上校是诚实的。我营官兵认为，负责向《大美报》发信的人一定是被某些人利用以达到某种不可告人的目的，从而损害了我们孤军的光荣历史，并间接损害了国家的声誉。

“为了揭露奸徒的阴险计划，我们特此发表此声明以告公众。”

January 16, 1939.
Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Pao

THE PAY AND RATIONS OF THE LONE BATTALION

The members of the Lone Battalion who defended the Joint Savings Society Godown stubbornly last year withdrew into the International Settlement on the advice of a third party, and since then, they have been accommodated in the Kiaochow Road Park. Although they have lost their freedom for the time being, the people of Shanghai are much interested over the welfare of these loyal and brave men.

The other day, this paper received a letter said to have been issued by the officers and men of the Battalion of the 88th Division. The letter contains the following allegations:- "The commander-in-chief of the No. - War Zone has issued a reward of $3,000 to the Lone Battalion. This money has been unequally distributed among the soldiers. The National Government has issued four months' pay and rations, but the soldiers have received pay and rations for only two months. Furthermore, the account for monthly food expenses is also not clear."

It appears that the letter is directed against Colonel Zia Tsing-yuan (謝晉元). As Colonel Zia, who is a revolutionary soldier, would never commit any acts of corruption, this paper yesterday detailed one of its reporters to call on Colonel Zia. (Colonel Zia is suffering from insomnia and is being treated in the Police Hospital.)

Interviewed, Colonel Zia made the following statement:- "Four company commanders were responsible for the distribution, according to rank, of the reward issued by the commander-in-chief of the No. - War Zone. I took no part in the distribution. At first, Mr. O.S. Lieu (劉鴻生) detailed certain persons to make contracts for food supplies and the monthly expenses required in this connection were estimated at $4,000. Dissatisfied with the bad food supplied, the officers and men took over the job themselves and were given $3,000 a month. As the food is now better, no complaint has been heard. With the exception of a part of the money spent for clothes, the subscriptions from various circles are being deposited in a bank. The National Government has issued four months' pay and rations through the Shanghai District Association, but the latter has handed to us only two months' pay and rations, the remaining $11,000 have not yet been delivered to us."

Colonel Zia refused to make a statement on the circumstances surrounding the affair. It is to be noted that the Shanghai District Association is a bona fide public body. We hope that the persons responsible for the administration of the association will give an explanation of the matter so as to avoid misunderstanding.

1939年1月16日。
上午译文。

《大美报》

孤军的薪饷和口粮

去年顽强保卫四行储蓄会仓库的孤军成员，在第三方的建议下撤入国际租界，此后一直安置在胶州路公园。虽然他们暂时失去了自由，但上海市民非常关心这些忠诚勇敢者的福利。

日前，本报收到一封据称由第88师某营官兵发出的信件。信中包含以下指控：“第-战区司令长官向孤军颁发了3,000元奖金。这笔钱在士兵中分配不均。国民政府发放了四个月的薪饷和口粮，但士兵只收到了两个月的薪饷和口粮。此外，每月的伙食费账目也不清楚。”

看来这封信是针对谢晋元上校的。鉴于谢上校作为一名革命军人，绝不会做出任何腐败行为，本报昨天特派一名记者拜访谢上校。（谢上校患有失眠症，正在警察医院接受治疗。）

谢上校在接受采访时发表了以下声明：“第-战区司令长官颁发的奖金由四位连长负责按军衔分发。我没有参与分发。起初，刘鸿生先生指派专人签订食品供应合同，由此产生的每月费用估计为4,000元。由于对提供的劣质食物不满，官兵们自行接管了这项工作，每月获得3,000元。由于现在的食物较好，未听到任何抱怨。除部分用于购买衣物的款项外，各界捐款正存入银行。国民政府通过上海区协会发放了四个月的薪饷和口粮，但后者只交给我们两个月的薪饷和口粮，剩余的11,000元尚未交付给我们。”

谢上校拒绝就此事的相关情况发表声明。值得注意的是，上海区协会是一个合法的公共机构。我们希望该协会的管理负责人对此事作出解释，以避免误解。
